article: I stand where many of my species stood before. Concrete canyons litter the deserted metropolis reaching fair into the sky, men, women, and children all lay on the freezing ground, left alone to die, not cared for, no space for them in a grave, like they were a meaningless object. Forests once vibrant with broad wildlife are now filled with death and dusk that I have caused. Through the madmen that once called themselves "Scientists" I was forged. Deep down in underground laboratories. They were once work spaces, where hundreds of people came to carry out their job. Now they're a mere metal graveyard. Through my fault I have destroyed this once thriving planet. I was the carrier, I am the carrier, I will remain the carrier, of the plague that ended planet Earth. No one is here anymore. Only me. I can go anywhere, do anything, but no living thing can accompany me, no one to care for me, no one I can care for either. Humanity never knew if there was life beyond our planet. And if there wasn't, well I am the only living thing to exist at this moment. Feels strange, like I shouldn't be the one to take on this role, like it's not my body. The planet will most likely die soon. And with it, me. The forests are dying, not being pollinated by bees. The very lungs of the Earth are decaying and I can't do nothing but wait and until that time comes, Only me and silence remains...

article: Dr. Pepper watched his patient fidget on the table. "Give it to me straight Doc, do I have a problem? " , the man bobbed his knee. Frankly the Coke addiction could've been classified as just a "problem" months ago, now it was a life-threatening affliction. He was skinny as a rail and his breathing sounded like an old labrador retriever. "You do have a serious problem, Mr. James. The good news is, its never too late." It was probably too late. "Aw that's great doc, so what..... Rehab? " , James scratched his head. This is my favorite part. "Be honest, have you tried rehab already?" Pepper smirked to the rim of his lenses, he knew the answer fully well. Kevin James had been to two local clinics. Both were cheap concrete dungeons constructed in the 20s (though one hadn't been finished till after the depression). Government funded, with only the business of penniless losers who were kidding themselves if they thought they could stay sober over a week. James told of his last 3 visits, which he mostly accepted because his mother threatened to kick him out. To his credit he came close to a week his second time. "But it's not my fault, I can't afford any of those fancy uh retreat-like places." "Then maybe it's time for something new James. Something you don't have to pay for." "What's that?" Pepper reached back into his trousers, and pulled out the lukewarm tonic. "This, Kevin, is what I'm talking about." The glass bottle didn't sparkle or shine, but the syrupy liquid fizzed from the inside, preparing to burst on an unsuspecting victim. "It doesn't smell too good." "Most medicines don't Kevin," Pepper reminded him. "Well Mr. P, even if it tastes about as bad as it smells, it'll be worth it. Being Coke-free, that's priceless, right?" "Not quite, obviously there has to be some contribution on your part, Mr. James." "Like, a lot of effort and shit?" "More like..... 8 bucks at Walmart."

article: I never really liked sports, you'd probably say. But my dad..... he's always wanted me to play whatever sports would get me into the big leagues. He always said that he almost got into a college team but that an injury during a game ruined his chances. I doubt that I'll get onto the team but..... That was the prayer I said to myself the week before tryouts. I'd been made to play football all my life because Dad wanted me to get into the NFL, but it wasn't for me. No, he had always wanted to live out the glory days he didn't get, the days and success and money that he thought were owed to him since high school. I only went along with it because it was the only chance to earn his respect - he outright punished me for trying to focus on something other than a sport I had no respect for. So, imagine my surprise when, before I even climbed into bed during my little prayer, the ground started shaking and I was standing in a golden and marble palace in the middle of a cloudy landscape with men and women with white wings and ornate armor standing around me. I think I'm the only living person to drop the F-Bomb in Heaven. Then..... I met Him - the One and Only. It turned out that I was the only living being who could even look upon him or hear him. It also turned out that if anyone else did so they'd die instantly and that caused him to retreat from the world until I was born. So, he asked me to help him get up to speed with the world, and then gave me a reward - he'll answer my prayers and only my prayers until the day I died. He then helped me grant my wish and I got onto the team. However, he was also upset about all kinds of atrocities committed in His name and was kind of a vindictive dick. Do you want to know how he granted my prayer? He took the souls of several of the best pro players in the history of the sport, and some warriors or other notable people who had never played football, some I think were Greek Heroes like Heracles, stripped them of their thoughts, memories and talents of everything except the sport (and how to speak French, surprisingly) and basically stitched them onto my soul like Frankenstein's Monster. While I was asleep for one night, I was actually forced to play the game for over a millennium, one person with imps versus the most powerful creatures in Hell. And that's just what he did to me. This one student, who was a shoe-in for getting onto the team, always said that it was God's will that he was so good at football, so he thought that it was appropriate that he could physically abuse other students and sleep with whoever he wanted. While I didn't think that being crushed into a paste was a good way to die, I did have to admit that I didn't feel sorry for him when I found out that he was chasing after a girl he was trying to rape. He outright said,'That was me, by the way,' as if it was nothing. Then I discovered that some of the donors were still alive, killed just for my wish. Some had heart attacks like a linebacker for the New York Giants, others were not so lucky - one of the best coaches in the sport died in a way you'd only see in the Final Destination movies. Yet, all I cared about was making the team even with all of the guilt. It was now instinct for me to play. I was easily the best student in the school. Of course, you can't be good at a sport like football if you can't take a beating. From the time I had gotten onto the team in Freshman year onward, I had swollen up like a balloon. By the time I graduated with a perfect win record, I went to just over 5 feet and extra-skinny to just under 7 feet and making everyone around me look like dwarves. I had also been tested over 1,000 times for doping, even being the one they tested new ways of finding steroids on. I'm definitely pretty sure that He had also made a rule change so that I wouldn't be banned for being too big. And in the event that someone had managed to injure me? Well, guess what? It wasn't permanent, just moved over to another person and caused all kinds of horrible damage to them. Of course, the rules are that you can't play if you don't have a minimum C grade in all classes..... so He made me smarter. I had gone from straddling the C-margin to having over 100 PhD's' worth of knowledge forced into my mind. I never studied but always knew the answers. Guess how many had to die for that one? Yet, my dad, the only person who I wanted to earn the respect of, died before my last High School championship game. I didn't really feel anything for his death. In fact, school, college, football..... they were things that I had to endure - no effort, no sense of victory. After the first game, it was all just a sense of boredom, so I quickly learnt how to fake my emotions. By the time I finished college and earned 30 PhD's to my name, I was known as the Juggernaut and for good reason - easily 10 feet tall and a mountain compared to anyone else. Nobody was foolish enough to go against me. In fat. I had to wear protective gear so that other players could be safe if they didn't get out of the way fast enough. By the time I wanted to retire at 40, somehow now at 20 feet, people had soon found confirmed evidence that I could talk to God, even getting the ability to call forth angels from Heaven and freely wander into it. It was part of the bastard's plan all along. He wanted someone who could speak to me to become high profile so that more people would believe in Him. He had lied about me being the only person who could speak to Him. He did it at the time I was going to retire from Football. He had engineered everything, from my birth to my success at Football, because he wanted someone who could be His agent on Earth. Of course, humans could naturally rebel against him, but the bastard child of an Angel and a Mortal, say, a giant..... I was never a Catholic but that didn't stop them from proclaiming me the new Pope. They had to build a throne for me, and travelling for official duties without my powers would be a bitch otherwise..... I also had to wear the traditional clothing and those weird red shoes as well, but being a giant meant that when I held Mass no-one couldn't hear me. I also didn't need the Swiss Guards - well, not for myself - but at the same time, I felt less in control and more like being a puppet. I expected to die and become a legend when my predecessor took over..... But that day never came. I grew older, wiser and somehow more in control, possibly as if I was growing into the role I was assigned. I didn't feel the nagging or itching from when I was first forced into the role, I didn't feel like my limbs were moving by themselves. As more and more people grew to worship Him, he felt less-inclined to strike the world with natural disasters, instead helping humanity grow and prosper. And I grew older, stronger, larger, wiser..... until I had managed to negotiate more powers for the Church until I was the Ruler in the Physical Realm. By the time the Unification was complete, the Empire had now expanded into the Cosmos. I toured along the habitable worlds to spread His Message, nurturing Mankind for the last 50,000 years. He manipulated me and for that I'll never forgive Him. But..... it's the only time I've ever been genuinely happy, and I can tell He isn't lying when he said that it wasn't His creating my mind that decided that. I just wish he stopped having a pissing contest about how big I am. So what if I'm about 500 cubits bigger?

article: Jodie - I hope this letter finds you in perfect peace. I hesitated to even mail this to you, but felt you deserved this at the very least. I want you to know that I'm not contacting you in order to cause emotional friction, or to stir up past emotions and rip away at old wounds. Though I fully understand that while my intent may not be such, the consequences of contacting you may result in just that. I spoke to Ralph a couple of months ago, that in itself was unexpected. He seemed sincere in his apology, but I've learned that liars are good at their craft. I thought you should know that your destruction still very much runs deep in my life. These words are hard to write but necessary. I do not forgive you, and I surely do not forgive him. I am broken woman because of the selfishness that the both of you had. With no disregard to my wellbeing you stripped from me the very essence of vulnerability. I've tried to will myself to find a concern in my heart about my grandson, but when I think of him all I can feel is the hatred I have for both you and Ralph. Family ties are mere exaggerated lines, they can be blurred and they do disappear. Ours do not exist. Your son is my grandson by standards of society, but in my life he is the bastard child that you and Ralph produced in spite of my love for the both of you at that time. I've waited this long to contact you and I doubt I ever will again. I'm older, and I figured for my own resolve I'd say what I needed to say. You are not my daughter.

article: "Well, damn." I said aloud. Of all the banks I had ever come across, this one was by far the hardest to rob. In fact, it seemed to be next to impossible. But I wasn't about to give up just yet. I needed to come up with a new plan, one that was foolproof. I sat down on a nearby bench and pulled out a notepad and pen. As I thought of ideas, I wrote them down, crossing out the ones that seemed too risky or improbable. After a few minutes, I finally had a plan that I was confident would work. I stood up and made my way back to the bank. As I walked, I rehearsed the plan in my head, making sure I had every detail memorized. When I arrived at the bank, I put on my best innocent face and approached the teller. "Excuse me, ma'am, I seem to have lost my ID. Is there any way you could assist me?" I asked, hoping to gain her sympathy. The teller looked at me skeptically. "I'm sorry, sir, but we can't let you access your account without proper identification." I nodded and sighed, acting defeated. "I understand. Thank you for your time," I said before turning to leave. But just as I was about to walk away, I stumbled and fell, spilling the contents of my bag all over the floor. The teller rushed over to help me, and while she was distracted, I slipped a small device onto the computer screen in front of her. I quickly gathered my things and left the bank, confident that my device would allow me access to the bank's security system and unlock the vault. I would be back later that night to retrieve what I needed. Sure enough, that night, the vault was mine. With the help of my trusty device, I was able to get in and out without being detected. article: it's short and I haven't read Gatsby in a while, but I'll give it a shot. In her smile was an uncertainty he could not stomach - in that moment, Gatsby must have felt the cold wind brush him back to grotesque reality. He looked upon her soft, velvet gaze as though it was his very undoing. Years spent in disillusion, convinced the eternal truth was clear to see and perhaps it was, to all but him, simply a passing pleasantry. The gentle words slipped from her pursed lips, ebbing over Gatz' head and pulling him under. Under the tide Gatsby saw the face of a younger man - bold, handsome, and innocent. His own finger traced the small crevices of his aged self, every one a day passed in lonely pining. Gatz' eyes flared, and in them were pretences of wealth and power. The images of her world became his seamlessly, desire begetting deceit. Those eyes struck fear into the heart of Gatsby - in them he saw his past and his future, shaped from the fabrications of a young mans lust. He must have recoiled as he saw Gatz die, extinguished of his own will. He must have looked upon the scene as a small prologue to the parties and the frivolity and the automobiles. I'd like to think that his mind was made, but I have my doubts. Such is the dream that it may never truly be shaken free - the light across the bay would continue to glow green, one more enchanted object ripped from the past enchanted no more. Gatz and Daisy broke away. Gatz returned to Camp Taylor. Daisy sat in the garden for an hour before returning inside. Gatsby waited in the garden until the memory was faded. She turned out her light at four, and he made his way back home.

article: Ever wake up and just know it's going to be one of those days? You know the kind, the one where you sleep through your alarm clock, the shower seemed to change to bipolar settings overnight (either Mordor hot or deep-space cold), you spill coffee on your freshly ironed work clothes and the dog used the kitchen floor as a latrine. It was one of those days. I couldn't find my keys, I was late to work and Bigglesworth had gotten out again. I don't know how he does it, he can't find his way out of a blanket let alone a house. I do, however, know why. He does it to mock me, why else would he meow outside the window and run away the second I see him? I never wanted a cat, but my last boyfriend thought an obligation would serve as a better anniversary present rather than a ring. But of course, I'm happy he didn't get me one of those, I suppose it should have been a sign. What kind of person buys their girlfriend a twelve year old cat from the pound for their fifth anniversary? Around the time I was pulling my burnt toast from the toaster, I got a call from work, asking where I was. At the time, I worked at a restaurant as a cocktail waitress. I was late for my evening shift and Manager Nicholas Blakeslee (of whom we called Dickless Flakeslee behind his back) was more than upset about being an hour late. I know, I know, sleeping in and missing the 5pm deadline for work is hardly piteous, but like I said, it was one of those days. I cursed the charcoalized toast, tossed it, flipped off Bigglesworth who sat perched in the neighbor's yard, leaving a peanut sized present for my passive-aggressive-note-leaving-neighbor, Candace, and ran towards the bus stop. And would you believe it, it started raining. It was something from a comedy, I looked about, searching for hidden cameras, waiting for Ryan Seacrest to jump out of a bush and shove a microphone in my face. I missed the first bus, ignored Ol'Dickless's calls and waited in the rain. I wasn't sure how I was going to work in sopping wet clothes, but then again I didn't want to get my hopes up about that: judging by how the day was going, I wouldn't be surprised if my blouse spontaneously combusted. That's where you showed up. I didn't see where you came from, it seemed like you appeared at my side, umbrella out and an inviting smile on your face. You were on your way home from work. You wore a casual suit, a deep blue deepened by the weather, a white collared shirt, a tie the color of cotton candy and rain boots. Those stupid rain boots. That was the first thing I ever gave you shit for. Actually, if you remember, that was the first thing I said to you. " Rain boots are kind of an odd accessory to you outfit. " Your laugh matched your easy smile, you nodded your head and conceded, then went on to ask how my feet were getting along knowing full well my black flats housed their own oceanic microcosm. That was the first time we met, we both skipped the next bus and haven't looked back. I look back on that day and thank God for losing my keys, for sleeping it and even for that poop factory Bigglesworth. I love you and I can't wait to spend the rest of my life with you.
label: human

article: " Yes, I can hear you, " came a soft voice much like my own. I looked around but found no one there. I brushed it off as hearing things. But as I took a few more steps I heard it again. nbsp; " I said I can hear you. " Came the voice, louder this time, but still retaining it's gentle nature. I looked around once more. There was no one near me. The house was empty. I spoke into my own head, feeling slightly silly as I did. nbsp; " Hi? " I thought. I wondered what could be causing this? Had I finally gone off the deep end or was I about to find out I had an new allergy I never even knew about. nbsp; " Hi, " replied the voice a few moments later. I couldn't deny it, it was coming from my head. I shook a little at the thought. nbsp; " Who are you? " I asked, before instantly feeling silly. Why I am asking myself who I am? nbsp; " I don't know, " the voice responded. I paused for a few moments, unsure of my next move. How do you react when you are talking to yourself but don't seem to know the answers to the questions you are posing? nbsp; " Well this has never happened before, " I thought to myself, only to be interrupted by the voice once more. nbsp; " Well I haven't been around before. I just started. " It replied. I was confused, to talk to yourself is one thing, but to interrupt yourself during the conversation is a whole new level of madness. After a few moments of silence, the voice spoke up again. nbsp; " I'm a part! " It exclaimed. It's voice showing a solid emotion for the first time since it started talking. nbsp; " A part? " I asked, slightly confused by what it meant and slightly distracted by trying to remember the number of my doctor. nbsp; " Remember? We learned about it in psychology class, " continued the voice, talking over my attempts to find the number. I thought about it for a moment and suddenly it flooded back into my head, like it was almost fresh. The boring classes on Richard Schwartz and his idea that people were made up of little bits. My train of thought was cut off by the voice speaking once more. nbsp; " But if I am a part, what part am I? " It mused, leaving me unsure if it was asking a rhetorical question or not. " Could I be an exile? Running away from something we didn't like? " It rambled. I found myself trying not to think so as not to interrupt. nbsp; " No, I don't feel like an exile, anyhow exiles don't just walk back in. That never happens in any story, apart from that game we played that time. But that is because Alice forgot she was playing an exile. " It finished. It was weird hearing this new voice talking about memories from years ago. But as it did, I felt the memory come to the forefront of my mind, like I was remembering it myself. I smiled at the memory, I had forgotten those silly games we used to play. I had forgotten Alice, work had gotten on top of me since I moved and I never found the time to call her. nbsp; " Well, I doubt I can be a firefighter. I never really had the looks for it, " the voice started again. " I mean being a firefighter suggests I am good in a crisis. But, I would think a part that was good in a crisis wouldn't pop up and scare you half to death. " nbsp; " You didn't. Don't worry. " I thought, trying to reassure whatever this voice was. nbsp; " I can hear your thoughts you know. I heard you mentally rehearsing the call to the doctor. " The voice replied. I shuffled awkwardly, realizing my thoughts about it had not been dramatically positive. " It's okay, I would do the same if I was in your position. Because I am you, so I can't pretend like I would think differently. " It said, a slight touch of humour coming into it's voice. I smiled and nodded. nbsp; " Well I can't think what part you are, " I thought. nbsp; " Maybe we don't need to know yet? Maybe I just popped out at random? " The part replied. I nodded to myself and the self inside myself. It had a point, I mean psychology was never exact. I smiled, I remembered my professor saying that. I smiled some more as I remembered another friend dropping psych the second they could, they couldn't handle the non-exact sciences. nbsp; " Yeah. That could be it. " nbsp; " Well then. I guess I should follow the model right? " It said. And I quickly remembered the model. I hadn't thought about it for years, but it felt like yesterday. I could almost smell the classroom, the memory was that fresh. nbsp; " Become part of the whole again, " I recited, " Until reality and your role clash once more. " I sat down and smiled as I remembered a few more of my school buddies. nbsp; " That is exactly it. " replied the voice. " So I guess I'll be seeing you? Or hearing you at least. " It said. I laughed a little and nodded. nbsp; " See you around, " I thought. I sat there in silence for a little bit. My head quiet once more. I got up from the chair and smiled, still basking in the glow of the memories that had resurfaced. I moved to my computer, I had a few people I needed to catch up with.

article: Day One: Today is my first day out here. This is bullshit, the Tribunal knew that I was innocent. Though, the public would've been furious if I walked away from it. I should still be there, within the city walls. Safe. I guess this isn't so bad. At least they left me with a days food and the means to defend myself. There are others. Most of them travel in packs, it's safer that way. With everything in this damned jungle, it'd be nice to have someone to watch my back. Anyway, I doubt I'll stick with this stupid book, and I need to get a move on. Day 400 (?) I heard the chopper blades, then came the sirens. They're calling me back. This has to be a trick. Yes, they're trying to kill me. They're mad that I'm still alive. They're mad that I'm thriving out here. Or.... Or maybe they've realized their mistake. Maybe they're bringing me back to apologize. Maybe I can go back home. Maybe that isn't a good idea. I've been out here so long, I've learned to survive. How am I supposed to survive in a civilized world? Besides, these people need me? I've grown to be a leader. I've protected them from the deadly creatures of the night, and even the people. Cannibals, tigers, thieves, bears, you name it, I've seen it all. I think I've been out here too long. I think I might be too far gone. There's no way that I can go back to the way things were. The outside, it changes people, and I think it's time to show them that. This is my first response on here, please give me some feedback. Thanks!

article: INT. FOYER - DAY Rain pours down outside. WILLIAM stands at the credenza, pouring himself a high ball of scotch. VERONICA sits on the divan, perfect posture, reading. WILLIAM Turquoise. (smirks) Very specific. Veronica lowers her book slightly. VERONICA Sorry darling? WILLIAM I never mentioned the color. Veronica runs a gamut of emotion with her eyes: guilt, denial, contempt, coyness..... WILLIAM Have you anything to say? VERONICA A lucky guess. WILLIAM Will Remy have the same to say? VERONICA How should I know? William smirks again and shakes his head. He sips his drink. Veronica raises her book back up and turns the page. A BUSINESS CARD falls out onto the divan. CLOSE UP on card. It says'Harson Bros. Inc.' FULL, INDICATIVE VIOLIN NOTE. Veronica panics and stuffs the card away. The double doors by the spiral staircase open and the MAID steps in. WILLIAM I'm not hungry! Tension fills the air. A beat. The doorbell rings. The maid gasps. Veronica gasps. William throws his head toward it and seethes. MAID I'll get it. The maid moves slowly toward the door. Veronica stands, nervous. William grabs a cane from the coat rack and wields it readily. The maid opens the door. It's TERRENCE, soaking wet. article: Survivor bias. After the happening, there was much excitement and fear over mankind's new power. Pundits and preachers alike screamed the world was headed to hell within a week. As time passed, however, it became clear that the world did not descend into chaos as predicted. This is an example of survivor bias, where the only information available is from those who survived the event and not from those who did not. It is important to take a broader perspective and consider all possible outcomes, not just the ones that we are aware of. This can help prevent us from making erroneous conclusions and can help us make more informed decisions going forward.

article: As world champion, it was said to be a very great honor to visit the president of the United States. Kenji was not so sure. He thought that he would be bigger, stronger. More formidable. But the man he saw looked as though he could be blown over by a strong wind, and even members of Kenji's entourage could have pushed this tiny man out of a ring. Still, he supposed that he, himself, would not want the responsibilities of being a leader, and perhaps you had to be small to desire such things. Surely, one should want to be a leader in order to do so well. But most of all, Kenji was bored. His expensive tailored suit was not very comfortable, and while he supposed he looked good, he felt more at home with less on. Kenji began scanning the crowd. He was certain he would be the biggest and strongest man there, but perhaps someone could pose a challenge. He had wrestled with several Americans during the world championships, and one of them had been quite good. Not good enough, but better than many others he had wrestled. Most Americans seemed so small. Everyone says that Asians are small, but they seemed no different than the Americans to Kenji, and they all looked the same. His older brother traveled a lot, for business, and he had said as much but deep down Kenji had always assumed he was just trying to posture himself as well-traveled. One man caught his eye. He was not especially big, but he looked different from the rest. He was not well-dressed, like Kenji, but he was over-dressed all the same. Wearing a heavy jacket, yet it was not cold out. In fact, Kenji had been drenched in sweat since donning the suit. The man did not seem- well, he did not know if he could say that the man did not seem bothered by the heat, the man seemed distressed, but did not seem to be suffering from being overheated. His behavior was strange. Kenji looked around. How did nobody else seem to notice this man, and his odd dress and behavior? Did he only seem strange because Kenji was an outsider? Surely a strange man was strange whether he was strange in Japan or here, in America. Kenji sighed. He did not come all the way out here to listen to a stick man speak for some time and to observe strange Americans. His translator had apologized for not being able to keep up with the president's speech, and Kenji had grown tired of his paraphrasing. The strange man with the large brown coat began moving in the crowd. Kenji's eyes followed the man as he bumped into others, who occasionally muttered and offered mild protests. He was approaching the podium. Kenji recalled that the president was supposed to have some of the best guard forces in the world, surely this man would have attracted attention by now. He could see the men he presumed were Secret Service, but they did nothing- they merely stood before the podium, looking out at the crowd. Kenji furrowed his brow. The odd man was getting closer now. He was nearing the edge of the crowd, and the only thing separating him from the podium would be the rows of seating. Kenji was in the third row, and due to his respectable girth, he had opted to sit on the outside edge. As the man cleared the crowd and Kenji finally got a clear look at him, the man's jacket opened briefly. His powerful, insatiable stomach dropped away within him: he saw wires, tape, and what appeared to be blinking LED lights beneath the mean's jacket. The man continued on his approach to the podium, but Kenji was resolutely certain that this stick-man president's loyal guards would attend to the mad-man before things went out of hand. Surely it was under control. America was a respectable nation, after all. As the man passed by, the scent of chemicals, burnt plastic, body odor and old sweat filled Kenji's nostrils. It was the smell of a man with a sick mind. He reached the first row of seats and having done so, spread his arms wide, as if to imitate the Jesus that Americans worship. Kenji knew what had to be done. "Sore wa bakudandesu!" Kenji rose swiftly, and ripped his shirt and jacket from his torso in a single mighty swipe with both of his hands. The strange man turned to see the mighty Kenji, who threw himself at this foul, strange, sad man with no mercy. As he fell into the man, he knew that he might be sacrificing himself for the stick-man president, and for the others who had come to listen to him yap that day. He had wished he could continue to be champion for some time to come, until he had fathered enough children to guarantee that one of them might be world champion one day, like him. But it would not be. He would give his life to save the American president. He would die with much honor. Kenji opened his eyes. The strange man's skin had gone a shade of deep purple. His eyes were bloodshot, and all of the veins stood out on his face, frozen in a gape of terror, a cry of fear never having had the chance to leave his mouth. Kenji was surrounded by men, many of whom had their guns drawn. Stupid men, of course now they have their weapons ready. Kenji struggled to get up, but finally rose to one knee, and stood above the strange, crushed man on the ground. Whatever electronics he had hoped to use to trigger his explosives were no match for the might of one Kenji Aoyagi, and had been smashed into smithereens. The blinking lights blinked no longer, and several bits of plastic had become stuck, imprinted into Kenji's ample and vigorous belly. The American stick president approached, through the circle of armed men. He locked eyes with Kenji, nodded, and said, "Hello. Domo..... ahh..... domo arigato." He then bowed before Kenji, who respectfully returned the bow. Perhaps America was worthwhile after all.

article: "They have absolutely no regard for civilization! They are degenerates and criminals who think they have some ridiculous right to self-determination! This rebellion will accomplish nothing aside from destroying families and obliterating progress for the next decade!" The Terran captain's rage continued to pour over the comms until the Martian commander suddenly shut it off. "Figures we weren't able to intercept any channel that's useful." Martian Commander Olsen stared through the glass that separated the bridge from the unforgiving void - her eyes already weary from the events leading up to this moment. Olsen glanced over to her executive officer, who made no attempt to hide the disquietude exuding from his expression, "Relax a little, we're making the right decision." "I - I know, but our lovely friend over there has a point. Our choices are going to huge impact, and not all of it will be pleasant," his voice grave mixed with a hint of sarcasm. "You're right - we are destroying an interplanetary empire," she returned the humor. "But they are exploiting us," her tone switched swiftly. "We are living miserably so they can live comfortably. Any chance at a peaceful resolution is slim, and that's something we have known since the beginning. We exhausted many peaceful options, but we need to strike before they can prepare for a revolution" Her somber eyes began scanning the blackness in front of her, seemingly expecting to see something, "The ambush is going to take place with at least a couple of kilometers of space in between us. We won't see anything" The Terran navy was not much of a navy, but more of a large task-force designed to combat ill-equipped pirates. The majority of their ships were fast, well-rounded, and incredibly effective. They were a dangerous foe the infant Martian navy needed to carefully counter. The revolutionaries spent years setting up a honeypot - a large, decoy pirate organization, and now an ambush that spent years in the making was about to come to fruition. The Martian fleet was barely inside of the Terran fleet's sensor range - their ships tightly packed around the trap carefully set by the Martians. "Three minutes until we are within range," the XO stated calmly over the intercom, his fear and doubt hidden well from the crew. The haunting sounds of the ship's artillery moving into place reverberated throughout the quiet bridge. "I'm impressed the Terran captain picked up on the situation so quickly." Olsen said, as if distancing herself from his imminent fate. The commander took control of the comms and broke the radio silence among their fleet, "All ships prepare to fire." The fifty Martian ships, jury-rigged with long-range cannons, were all within range and had their weapons prepped per the battle plan. The next few seconds crept by, every Martian aware of what was about to happen to hundreds of good people. "Fire."

article: " Going to bed early I think eh. You? " 7:52pm No way, I've got to study for that test on Thursday next week:' (. Enjoy your sleep I guess" 4 Unread messages 7:58pm HOLY SHIT BRANDON! Turn on the news now! " 8:01pm Brandon? " 8:02pm Brandon please tell me your door's locked" 2:18am Nevermind, its all sorted. " I blinked at my phone a couple of times. I really wanted to go back to bed, but my curiosity had been peaked. It was only 6:20 on a god damned Sunday morning, and it the morning light was starting to become a little harsh. Kyle's late night messages weren't really making any sense to my befuddled brain. Still, I made the effort of getting out of bed. I walked to the kitchen of my small (yet cozy) rental home, passing by my "Apocalypse Wall." On it hung the fire-axe, Glock, Remington, and hunting rifle I had prepared for the Apocalypse, should it ever arise. Most visitors saw it as a novelty thing. I assured them it wasn't. Strange, I thought. No newspaper this morning. I made myself a bowl of Hershey's cookies'n cream cereal (trust me, it is the shit), and started devouring it, keeping my complaints about the barbecue smell in the air to myself, when it happened. I looked up from my cereal, just for a second, when I then looked across the road through my window. In that moment, I made eye-contact with Kyle. Kyle, who was sitting on the lawn, with Josh, Dun, and Phil. Who were all holding hunting rifles or handguns. And they were talking and laughing. At 6:24 in the morning. My brain attempted to process this, gave up, and went back to the cereal. God it tasted good. Looking up again, Kyle was still there, along with everything else. So I walked into my front door step, and stopped. I was staring at Kyle, and the talk amongst them died down, until they were all staring back at me. This went on in silence for about two minutes. A tyre rolled past, but no one paid it any heed, much to the dismay of whoever rolled it. I would have considered the state of disorder in the street to have been caused by a street party, but there was just a bit too many burnt cars and unmoving bodies on the ground for it to have been that. I was still thinking of answers when it came to me as Dun broke away from the moment to fill a walking corpse with buckshot. yep, I thought. I missed the zombie apocalypse for sure. Kyle and the group continued watching as I screamed " GOD FKING DAMNIT" , and threw the bowl through the next door neighbour's front window. Edit 1: Content error

article: I had lived through the most stereotypical uni experience. I met her at the fresher's party. We got drunk. Danced. Snogged. And ended the night in her flat. I knew I liked her from the moment we locked eyes. I woke up before her and was looking at her face. I thought to myself, I'll never find anyone as beautiful as her again. She started to move, I pretended to go back to sleep. Didn't want her thinking I was being creepy. She got up and smiled down at me, " I knew you were staring, it was a little creepy " she said with laughter in her voice. I still had my eyes shut but started giggling. Yup, she was the one. That was 12 years ago. Since then, we'd been married and had two children. A boy and a girl. We were living the most typical suburban life imaginable. She worked as a journalist and I was a tax lawyer. It was good and peaceful. It was the day before my 30th birthday when we were out shopping for something that I can't even recall. She said she wanted to grab a coffee. I was a little annoyed as we were already late for the baby sitter but she assured me this was important. We got into Starbucks. I was about to walk to the counter to order the coffee she always orders, grande soy latte with an extra shot. But she told me to sit down, she was going to get it. As I sat, putting several bags full of purchases I would never use around my seat. I looked at her ordering the coffee and noticed for the first time just how stressed she was looking. She was gently rubbing her temple. That wasn't a good sign. That always meant she was thinking about something she wasn't entirely comfortable with. She came back with her drink and had ordered me a caramel macchiato. That wasn't right. I only drank Americanos or espressos. She sat down, not looking at me for a while. Just staring at the coffee lid and breathing. I finally gave in " what is it? why are you acting weird? " she looked at me blankly. She cleared her throat and said " I'm going to be direct. I've been seeing someone else for the past three years. I'm in love with him. He's met our kids. And I'm thinking...no, I'm going to be " she stopped as a single tear ran down her cheek. I felt like I'd been hit on the chest with a baseball bat. I felt winded. I felt a tightness in my chest and arm. I struggled to say anything. She went on " the kids are with him right now. I'm sorry. I'm...I'm leaving you. I'm sorry " I felt the tears stinging my eyes. I said the only thing I could " why? " she was wiping tears from her eyes now. She gave a sarcastic laugh. " Why? Why do you think? You haven't even noticed that I've been falling out of love with you for the past five years. After we had Gillian, I've just not been able to connect with you. I had to take a break from work, while all you did was work. When are you ever home Jack? When are you ever present in the moment. I met him. I started falling for him. I love him and I realised I haven't felt this love with you, ever ." I felt rage. I felt sorrow. I felt pity. I felt betrayal. It all started going dark. I felt myself slipping from my seat. My chest tightening so much, I couldn't get air in. My lungs burned and my arms felt heavy as lead. I fell to the floor but didn't feel it. I was just aware my view had changed. I was now looking at the lights on the ceiling. I was literally heartbroken. I could barely move my lips. But I was determined to get these words out. I coughed, more than whispered " never again...I will love...never again ." I didn't know where I was. I felt I was in a dreamlike state. I felt like I was walking on clouds. When I looked down. I realised, I actually was walking on clouds. I didn't know where I was walking towards. But just that I needed to walk forward and up those steps made out of clouds. I was looking around me in wonder. This was truly amazing, but where was I. Was I dead? I felt at peace, so maybe I was. I felt a light shining. It was so bright I had to put my hand up so I could still walk without tripping. Then I saw a shape bathed in the light. As I got closer, the shape started to become familiar. It was a woman. With long golden blonde, or wait was it auburn? No, I think she was a brunette. Every ray of light gave her hair a different colour. The closer I got, the larger she became. Until I was standing at the foot of a ten-foot-tall woman. She was wearing a robe with a gold coloured rope as a belt. Or was it a rope made of gold. She looked at me and smiled. I could try describing her beauty, but that would be an offense to just how beautiful she looked. She said " I hear a lot of people say they'll never love again, but only ever so often does someone mean it from their heart. And even more rare is it for someone to mean it not just for a woman, but for everything in existence " her breath smelled of roses. It was hard to pay attention to what she was saying. I was fascinated by how stunning she was. Her ruby red lips turned up at the corners just a little bit. She had the kind of lips that you imagine kissing, biting, savouring. I felt too intimidated to make eye contact with her. She continued " when you reject love with such fervour, you challenge my power. Do you think you're more powerful than the goddess of love? " I wasn't sure if that was rhetoric or if she meant that. But the way she had her hands on her hips made me think she was waiting for a reply. Even in a simple white robe, I could tell she had an amazing body. Her waist cinching in above her hips. There was a sweet smell, like milk and honey coming from here. Which was strange, even in these circumstances as I had no idea what milk and honey smelled like. I looked down and shook my head. She spoke with a booming voice this time " then take it back and submit to my authority. I'll walk with you on earth and make every woman you desire to fall in love with you. If you seek wrath then break their hearts if you must. If you seek lust, then you can have ten women in the bed with you, to do as you will. You can have anyone. You can even have me. All you have to do is bend down to me, get down on your knee and submit your love to me. Submit your soul " she took a pause and threw down a gold dagger at my feet " thrust that in your breast and ay these words aloud. Say that I am you god, I am the god of love and you give yourself to me, recognise no other, reject all else and belong to me, to have and to discard " I looked at the dagger and let her words run my imagination wild. More than the rest she'd promised, the most tempting was to have her. There was a feeling in the pit of my stomach that made me think that to have had her, I'd never desire anyone else ever again. Just a kiss would be worth the bargain she wanted. But then a flash of memory before my eyes. It was her. My wife. The love I'd felt and the pain that had left me here, wherever here was. And the stabbing pain started again. I felt my chest was filled with a current. I saw the faces of my children. My little Gillian and my superstar Daniel. I couldn't submit to this woman. The last woman I said vows to broke me and took my children. The children who'd also readily abandoned me for a stranger. I wondered if they were already calling him dad. Another piercing pain in my chest as if someone had jabbed a needle in my heart. Tears were running down my eyes. I held the dagger in my hand and shouted " NEVER. AGAIN " and threw the dagger at her with all my might. She screamed in such a high pitch that I had to shut my eyes. The light started blazing from here now. It started bright red, then orange and then pure white. I tried opening my eyes but the light was blinding. I wanted to move my hands to cover my eyes again but I couldn't feel my arms. I realised I was on my back. Where was I? it felt like a bed. The sounds around me started to swell. I could hear a lot of people and sound of beeping. There was a rushed discussion all around me. I could hear panic and concern. I tried to force my eyes open and see through the lights. The world slowly spun back into focus. I was on my back. The lights looked like the kind you see in an operating theatre. I tried to move my head but it hurt so much and it felt like it was constricted. I finally started recognising words " he's coming around " someone said in a panic. I heard someone shout " doctor can you please put him back to sleep, I'm doing the last sutures " what the hell was this man talking about. I was still struggling to see, all I could see was white. I heard the doctor, who I was surprised to realise was a female doctor. I could feel her glove covered hand gently stroking mine, she said " don't worry, we're all looking after you. I just need you to fall back asleep for a few more minutes and then I'll bring you a nice coffee to wake you up with. I'll bring some chocolate croissants as well, they're my favourite. Now, I don't know any lullabies, so you're going to have to just trust me and try to sleep ok " her voice was s soothing. I felt like I could trust her. So I closed my eyes and felt the clouds forming around me again, I was going back to sleep, but I was also going to go back to her. I felt her lifting her hand from me and would've grabbed it if I had any strength in my hands. That's when I surprised myself when I managed to grab the tip of her fingers. I heard her say " well if you insist. I'll sit right here while you have a little nap ok " she locked her fingers in mine and started to hum something. Whatever it was, was doing the trick. I was slowly back with her.

article: The tension in the air was so thick it was palpable. The scent of gunpowder and blood mixed together, causing the room to reek of death. Wolf stood by the wall of the tavern. He was cornered and he knew it as did the boy who he held with his arm around his neck. It's come to this, Wolf thought. It's been his most desperate moment since Fort Maynoor. Across the room from him were two young adults with their weapons drawn. only kids in his eyes. But despite their age, they stood before him on the opposite side of the remains of his entire gang. Some of the best outlaws and gunslingers he'd ever known all downed within minutes by these..... kids. One of which was only a girl. But it was mostly by her ability that the men he once rode, pillaged and murdered with we now lying in a pool of their own blood. And the only thing saving him from sharing their fate is the young Indian boy being held with one arm and a pistol to his head in the next. " Put him down! " The boy across the room yelled. Why a white boy would care som much about the Indian kid, he wasn't sure, but he understood. Despite the relation, it was too late now. " That's not gon na happen, boy. " said Wolf with a hopeless yet devilish grin emerging from his lips. There was silence for what seemed like an eternity until Wolf spoke up again. " It seems we have ourselves a bit of a..... predicament. " he chuckled. " I may not have much to live for, but I sure as hell ain't gon na die. " " Tough luck. " said Litonya, he revolver still aimed at Wolf. " Oh, there's only one person I'm referring to in this room and it sure as hell ain't you, bitch ." Litonya scowled in return. " No, no. It's you, Blondie. " he said, nodding to Sam. " What? " " The girl..... Bill's little love child..... she can't kill me. She knows it. She may only be half-blooded, but she knows her own customs. In fact, it's me who has the right to kill her! " " Molimo is not a part of this. It's just between you and me. " Litonya added. " Maybe not before but he is now! " Sam began to slowly position himself between Wolf and the door, not only to prevent his escape but to also find a chance take a shot on Wolf himself. The outlaw shifted himself to place his hostage between him and Sam. In that time, Litonya had an opportunity. The chance to take him out. The chink in his armor. It was the kind of vulnerability that she took advantage of in a hunt. Split the attention of the prey long enough to fire the killing arrow. It should have been simple, but this time was different. Litonya needed Wolf alive. As a fellow Miwok, she was her duty to protect her people and their customs. It was her responsibility to sacrifice herself to him and cleanse the sins of her father. But how could she? Why should she be forced to give up her life to this monster? All her life, her purpose had been clear. The needs of her people come first and above all else. She swore to defend the tribe traditions, no matter what the cost. To fail her duties is to no longer be Miwok. But the trail given to her was not clearly blazed. Now she faces her dilemma. Should she face her destiny and do what she'd been waiting so long to finish? Or should she take a new path, one away from Miwok tradition and stray from her intended purpose to save her new friends? Time to choose a side...

article: As he spun around I saw the blur of black that extended from his hand. I was confused, but not afraid. I did not have time for fear. I just reacted instinctively and dodged to the side, narrowly avoiding the black blur that seemed to be reaching towards me. As I moved, I realized that the blur was actually a long, slim sword, wielded by the man who had just attacked me. I quickly assessed my surroundings, looking for a way out of this situation, but the man was blocking my only exit. I shifted my weight onto the balls of my feet, preparing to defend myself, as the man lunged forward towards me with his sword. I leapt back just as his sword grazed past my arm, narrowly avoiding the sharp edge. I could tell that this man was skilled, and that I needed to be careful. As he continued to come at me, I tried to keep my focus on his movements, looking for an opening to strike. Suddenly, he spun around again, and took a swing at me from behind. Fortunately, I had anticipated his move, and managed to dodge his sword once more. I quickly turned to face him, my own fists clenched and ready to fight. The man continued to attack me relentlessly, his sword flashing through the air with frightening speed. But I refused to back down, each time managing to avoid his strikes and find new ways to counterattack. In the end, it was a single, decisive blow that won me the battle. With a swift movement, I brought my fist crashing down on the hilt of his sword, sending it clattering to the ground. The man had no weapon left, and without it, he was no match for me. As he stumbled backwards, I stepped forward and landed a final, crushing blow, knocking him to the ground. I stood over him for a moment, catching my breath and waiting for him to surrender. When he made no move to get up, I knew the battle was over, and I turned and walked away, victorious.

article: The news anchor's face was slick with sweat and his hands fidgeted uncomfortably. It was a remarkable departure from his usual six o'clock bulletin composure. The bulge of his adam's apple bobbed up and down as he swallowed. He began talking, his voice surprisingly steady despite his tense demeanour. He opened with the disclaimer that this was not a live broadcast, and that everything in this message had been recorded at the start of the year. He spoke of the rising tensions between the United States and the Sino-Russian federation, of the growing web of treaties and alliances on every continent, of the failed attempts by disarmament groups to curtail the exponential growth horde of nuclear stockpiles across the world. He spoke of religious fanatacism pushed to the limit, of mistrust and xenophobia reaching a fever pitch, of the frenzied hunts for oil reservoirs that grew more and more frequent as reserves steadily shrank. He spoke of a world balanced on the edge of a pinhead. "This message was recorded in case the worst should ever befall our nation," he said. "If you are hearing this, then fear has finally overcome rationality, and a nuclear war is already in progress. I repeat, if this message is being broadcast, our country is facing imminent destruction by nuclear weaponry. Most likely, the first strike has already been launched. "God willing, it was not our own who struck the first blow, and if it was, then may He have mercy on their souls." He swallowed one last time, and as suddenly as it began, the broadcast dropped off the air. Silence. The partygoers had each lapsed, one by one, into horrified, mute attention. Now that the broadcast was over, the abscence of noise in the apartment was quite profound. Then the screaming started. It was started by the young lady closest to the television set, then spread throughout the room like wildfire. There was a sound of a smashing glass dropped in disbelief, then a thud as the owner shortly followed it to the floor. One of the likely lads playing beer pong in the back flipped over the table and started smashing it apart with his forehead, bellowing incoherently. The screams and shrieks intensified in pitch as the host of the party ran towards the balcony and dove over the balustrade. article: "It's been three years since I made the promise to never fall in love again. Three years since Melissa broke my heart. I uh..... drank a lot. I slept a lot. And I thought about her. Sometimes. Well, no. I did that a lot, too." I paused, looking at the beautiful woman sipping coffee across the table from me. We were sitting outside, and her pale blond hair was flecked with fresh snowflakes. She looked heavenly. That was the only word for it. She had a delicate, ethereal sort of beauty, as if she didn't quite belong to this world. "It sounds like you really cared for her," she said, her voice gentle as a song. "But please, continue." I shrugged. "Not much more to it after we broke up. I practically fell apart. I..... well I got into this habit of roaming the streets downtown. I'm not quite sure why. Looking for a purpose, maybe. Sure. Maybe I was looking for company. Someone I might bump into, in a sea of strangers. And that's exactly what happened, I guess. I ran into you. And..... here we are. Telling each other our life stories over a cup of coffee." I spread my hands toward her. She smiled. "Anyways. I hadn't spoken to Melissa in three years. I'm doing pretty okay now, well at least I think so. But I can never forget the hurt I felt. Back then. And that's why I promised myself to never fall in love. Ever again." I paused, then added, " Ever. " Driving the point home. The woman nodded thoughtfully. She lifted the coffee to her lips and paused. "Your have a tragic story, for sure. But don't you think it's beautiful in a way? A classic tale of the cycle of love and heartbreak! Just wonderful." She laughed, and took a sip. "Is my story amusing to you?" I asked, lifting an eyebrow. I wanted to be angry at her, but it was hard when she practically looked like an angel. "I'm sorry," she said, still laughing. "But I don't believe that you've made a promise that you can keep." "Hmm." I stirred my coffee. "So what do you know about love then, huh? What makes you so optimistic?" "Sweetheart," she sighed. "I know all about love..... because I am love. Or rather you could say, the embodiment of love." I caught a twinkle in her eye. "You haven't asked me my name yet, you know. Too caught up in that little spiel of yours, I suppose." She smiled playfully. My cheeks somehow felt hot although it was freezing outside. "Ah..... you're right. I'm sorry, I uh..... haven't been on a date in a while. Ah..... what was your name?" "Why, I am Aphrodite, the goddess of love." "Aphrodite!" I laughed. Alright. I could play along. "Okay, I'll call you Aphrodite. I guess you really think of yourself as a love expert, yeah?" "I do," she said, her face completely serious. I couldn't tell if she was messing with me or not. "Which is why I know that you have a chance at love. You're young, handsome, a bit awkward perhaps..." she teased, "But charmingly so. You have a delightfully complicated love life. Truly, truly fascinating. But! Not a hopeless one. No, not at all." "I'm sorry," I said, draining the last dregs of my coffee. "But I've given up on love. Nothing you say will convince me otherwise." "Take a chance," she said, smiling. "Come back here, tomorrow. 12:30. And I'll change your mind." She winked, and before I could say anything, she was gone. I mean, literally gone. No smoke, or flash of light. I checked underneath the table, around the cafe, outside on the street. Nope. Gone. She had just blinked into nonexistence in front of me, leading me to wonder if she had ever even been real. "Aphrodite, huh?" I muttered. It was crazy, but I think I actually believed her. - I looked at my watch. 12:40. "Aphrodite" was nowhere to be seen. Okay. I decided to go order some coffee. I stood and went inside the cafe. A swirl of snow followed me through the door. "How's it feel out there?" The barista behind the counter. I looked up, startled. She was cute: dark, wavy hair and green eyes. Around my age. "Hmm. Beach weather," I said lightly. She laughed. It was a nice sound. "Hey, your hot date isn't with you today?" she asked, leaning over the counter, looking left and right. "She was supposed to I stopped and looked down at my watch. 12:43. Almost fifteen minutes late. "Yeah, nope. I don't think she's coming." "Aww," said the barista, smiling. "That's too bad. Probably shouldn't have suggested going to the beach." There was a hint of laughter in her eyes. "Wow," I said, raising an eyebrow. "You're a cheeky one." She grinned. We both jumped as the man behind me loudly cleared his throat. "Oh..... sorry, sir." He glared at me. "I'll um..... have a latte please," I said, turning back to the barista, who actually looked embarrassed. I counted out the money and handed it to her. She took it, scribbled something on my receipt, handed it back to me with the change. "What's this? Your credit card number?" I said, squinting at the receipt. She rolled her eyes. "It's my phone number, dummy." I frowned in mock disappointment. "Aww, damn it," I muttered, just loud enough for her to hear. She laughed. "Come again!" she yelled as I walked away. I couldn't help but smile as I looked down at the seven numbers scrawled hastily across the paper. I'd have to remember to make fun of her handwriting next time I saw her. I looked up and a woman waved at me from outside the window. "Aphrodite!" I said, as I pushed open the door. I had a million questions in my mind. "Last time..... you just disappeared..... how did "I told you who I was," she said, wrapping her coat more tightly around herself. "Did you doubt me?" "Actually yes." But I decided to drop the topic. It hurt my head too much to think about. "Anyways, you're here!" "Of course I'm here," she said, and winked knowingly. "Never going to fall in love again, huh?" I turned to the window and caught the barista's eye. She quickly looked away, cheeks flushed. "Oh shut up," I grumbled, turning back to Aphrodite. "It was just a talk. Love doesn't- it doesn't just happen like that." Then I froze in my tracks. "Wait a minute..... you arranged that? You made that girl talk to me?" "I didn't make anything happen, my dear." The goddess of love smiled at me. "I just made sure you were in the right place at the right time. As in..... right at the beginning of her shift. Say, did you remember to ask for the girl's name this time?" My heart dropped like a stone. "Damn it!" I yelled.

article: From atop Ayers Rock Australia seems red, endless and lifeless, like some displaced piece of Mars. "There's life everywhere," Alice tells me, gesturing at the desert. Her hat's made of serpent skin. Her own skin could just as well be, too. "Nasty, vicious life. Most of it is venomous or poisonous - I don't recall fhe difference, but most are both. Trouser snakes, anklebiter spiders, drop bears, stinger dingos, scorpion rats, vampire'roos - and get to the ocean, and the sea kittens will eat you alive." I shudder, and she leers at me. "The people ain't entirely harmless either." "W - what does this have to do with I wave a hesitant hand downwards. "Right. Keep up, I'll show you, London boy." And so I follow Ms. Springs of the Bushmaster Service to the depths of Ayers Rock, down a narrow tunnel, its walls full of aboriginal graffiti - skulls, screaming faces, dismembered corpses, people and animals running - warnings, or some forgotten prehistory of shock rock. The tunnel's end is dark, chill, and red. There are no wall-pictures in this hall, only irregular angles of rock, as if set down by a Mother Nature who didn't want to linger here. Then there's the door. "So you found this..." She - Alice - I'm unsure how formal I should be - shrugs. "Found, maybe thirty years ago. Told anybody..... there are strange types in the Service. Me, I heard about this last week, when Bruce vanished." "He's the, um, the one who went through this door?" She scowls, as if about to give me a dissertation on the local dearth of Bruces, and then nods. "Yep. And came back raving. Hair all white. Babbling, shaking, drooling, trembling - like a limey on vegemite, begging your pardon, sir." "Shush. And you..." "I looked in." She puts a hand on the doorknob. The door's metal, rust-red, and looks older than the Rock itself. "And it was like he said. So I thought, we need a special kind of a guy..." "And that's me." "Right. So, you ready, London boy?" "Show me." She swings the door open, and I see the truth about Australia, the reason why it is a desert of deadly things, dynamite fishers and trouser snakes and drop bears, all kinds of crazed, off monsters, full of malicious vitality. Ayers Rock isn't a rock at all. It's a vast, rust-encrusted, muck-covered, aeons-disfigured conning tower, and Australia is a UFO. "It makes sense," Alice Springs says behind me. "All the wildlife's as if designed to tell you to fuck off..... because it is."

article: We prepared for every eventuality. We walled the entire town with an impenetrable barrier only broken by a sturdy gate, manned 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Weapons stations were positioned every thirty feet, and every citizen carried at least one gun and one knife at all times. Food and water, blankets, generators, ammunition, medicines, barrels of gasoline, all were stored in secure underground bunkers. In fact, the only structures above-ground were watch-stations and training yards. All the rest was meticulously managed plots of land, already producing enough food to sustain the entire town, and rows upon rows of solar panels. A fully functioning sewage system was installed.Living quarters were located in a network of bunkers and corridors underground, fitted with air vents, air filters, and automatic locks timed to match our strict schedules. We drilled daily, and every person, child or adult, was rigorously trained and expected to adhere to the structure that the town ran by. Curfews were enforced. We were safe, completely sealed off from the outside world, save for a carefully monitored communications system, updating us regularly on the efforts of epidemiologists all over the world. We all took shifts in there, flagging the WHO's alerts of possible outbreaks of disease. We knew we were mocked, but we knew that in the end, we would be the ones with the last laugh. For all our preparation, though, it still took us by surprise. And I, I am the only survivor. This is my story. I shouldn't have survived, really. It was only chance that I was kept awake by nightmares, unable to find peace. I tossed in my ship-shape quarters long after the rest of the rest of the'town' was asleep. I could hear soft breathing from my neighbors; doors were impractical down here; we found what privacy we could behind curtains. Afraid of further nightmares, I slipped from my bunk, taking caution not to disturb the two others on the bunks below me. Company would distract me from the terrors in my subconscious, I remember thinking. So I padded through the corridors, my bare feet whispering on the grating beneath, to seek human comfort in the Communications shack. I punched my number into the code-box beside the only door in the entirety of the living quarters. The door opened with a hiss, and the rhythm of sleepful breath was replaced with the sound of gentle static and hushed conversation. The door closed quietly behind me. I was greeted with a nod by the man and woman on duty, but otherwise they paid me little heed. It was not uncommon for sleepless occupants to drift to the communications room at the darkest hours of the night. I regarded the screen idly. Nothing stirred, as usual. It was comforting to watch, assurance that we were safe. The woman broke me from my distraction. "You mind holding fort for us for a few minutes? We're going to make ourselves fresh coffees. Can bring you one too, if you like." I waved my hand in acknowledgement. She and the man exited the room, leaving me to keep an eye one the faintly flickering display. The time in the corner read 3:08. I must confess, I dozed a bit. The next time I looked, it was 4:21. I was alone. Even in the containment of the Communications room I could hear muffled noises from outside. The next shift should have been here twenty minutes ago. Could it be that I had missed the start of the zombie apocalypse? The rest of the town must have been industriously following procedure outside while I, alone and unnoticed, kipped in the safety of the locked room. Furious at myself, I snatched a gun from a rack on the wall, and, feeling ridiculous in my slightly-too-small pajamas, disengaged the lock to join the fray out-side. The muffled noises crescendoed into a thunder of sound. Gunfire deafened my left ear. This threw me, completely. I had expected orders shouted and people to be running to their stations. But not gunfire. Gun use was restricted to above-ground. In the confines of the bunker, the gunshots, so many as to be indistinguishable from each other, roared. I saw blood, heard screams; not the screams of adrenaline-pumped squadron leaders, but the unmistakable screams of dying men. I saw raging, relentless bodies thrown together, biting, clawing, scratching, tearing. The grid was sticky with blood, the air thick with the churning stench of bodily fluids, rent flesh, and sweat. I tore myself from my stupor, leaping back into the Communications room. The sudden silence was oppressive. My heart could not be tamed, nor my breathing stilled. My fingers, usually steady on the trigger, would not cease trembling. This shouldn't have happened. The apocalypse was supposed to happen outside, among the foolish skeptics that laughed at our preparations, not inside the fortress that was our town. My training told me to overcome my shock, to muster my courage, and to stand alongside my dying friends and send bullet after bullet into dead flesh. My limbs disobeyed. They scrabbled at the grating on the floor, and when it came up I threw myself into the space it offered. Had I followed my training, I would have died heroically and horrendously. I would have been shredded by cruel, mindless beings once my family. Instead I dragged myself down miles of pipe, sobbing the whole way, unable to erase bloody images from my retinas. When at last I crawled into clean moonlight I could only lie on the ground and stare back at the mighty walls of our town, our fortress. No my town. My fortress. Their tomb.

article: It was an infection. A pestilence from hell, a punishment of some sort. Some said it was the War that started it, others merely thought we were victims of some outside force. It was altering in a way that was completely indescribable, it was what a sour note looked like, if that made any sense at all. At first, it was easy to contain, it was like any other disease, quarantine those afflicted, burn the objects that were notably infused with the disease. It infected objects. That's when we began to realize that this was not a normal disease. The infected did not die, they did not even show symptoms of poor health, they functioned as normally as people could after being..... altered. Scientists of any field threw themselves into studying the phenomenon, hoping, praying for a solution. Politicians tried to calm the masses, "We're close to a cure, please be patient," they'd say. For a time, our world was united in a worldwide threat to normalcy. Then, we began to lose hope. We heard of places completely saturated in the disease, where almost nothing remained unstained. People were driven mad, seeing loved ones wear a completely different face. As all changes come that we do not choose, it came in force, there was no stopping it. Soon, we stopped trying. An entire generation had been lost by this point, an entire generation of children who did not know the peace of the old world, they only knew this new, wild, vibrant world. They didn't know the serenity we once had. Names began to form for the shades of this new spectrum. "Green" "azul" "rouge." We did not approve, but we did not stop them. The world was a different place. It is a different place. Though they may never know the joys of a perfect shale, or a crisp eggshell, they must find their own culture. This world of color was meant for an age not ours.

article: Daniel Wright slapped the Snooze button on the alarm clock as the radio advertisement was cut off by a breaking news item. His face remained buried in his pillow while his right arm reached for an empty half of the bed. Amber left six months prior, but his tired body hadn't yet let that fact sink in. His eyelids slowly lifted to soak in the harsh red LCD staring back at him, judging him. " Fine, " he conceded, flicking the alarm off completely while his legs reached for the carpet below. Light was attempting to intrude through a crack in the curtains. It seemed a little early for the sun, especially as autumn had finally arrived. Daniel paid no mind as he pulled the curtains back forcefully. The heat from the bright rays reminded him that he had removed his boxers in the middle of the night. It was too late to do much about it, so he stretched his arms before casually retreating from the perch. The TV blasted morning news when resumed from standby. Daniel wasn't fond of morning news programs, but he didn't find it troublesome enough to change the channel after the night game aired. " ...they're calling it the end- " The anchor was reading from an unseen prompt before the DVR played the penultimate episode of Breaking Bad. The single-serve coffee maker was already loaded with water. Daniel opened the cabinet to find a pod. He had finished the box of a disappointing house blend the previous morning. The next box to open was branded after a famous coffee-flavored liqueur. With a shrug, he loaded the pod and hit the button. The sweetness imparted by the alcohol flavoring blended with the bitter coffee for a surprisingly refreshing cup to enjoy alongside the show, which, again, was amazing. Daniel didn't bother to pack a lunch as the fourth Monday meant the cafeteria at the office would serve up meatloaf, one of the only things that kitchen could make properly. He slung his backpack over his left shoulder and made his way to the parking lot. Mrs. Rosen, the woman from 2-10, looked flustered when she saw him in the parking lot of the complex. Her eyes lowered towards his groin as her cheeks assumed a fiery tone. Daniel smiled weakly before hastening his trek. " Reactions now from our reporter in the field... " Daniel assumed that his radio reset itself again. The classic rock station frequency was still displayed in on the dash, but the news was not part of the morning programming. He tried his two backup stations. One was also spouting news while the other was just static. The CD player didn't let him down. He sang along with Bon Jovi as he sped along. Traffic was unusually busy as he made his way towards the city. The local Safeway appeared to be attracting nearly every car on the streets. Daniel had seen something like that before when they mistyped their fuel price and said they'd honor the 40-cent gallons for the rest of the day. He took a sip of his piping-hot flavored coffee and chuckled at the thought that whoever set the prices should have done the same. As he cleared the market, the cars, at least in his direction, were scarce. Despite the delay, he made it to the parking garage in near-record time. The echo of his car alarm arming hinted at the desolation. The Steelers played last night, so it wasn't that odd to see a number of folks show up late the next day. Daniel merely shrugged and took the elevator to the fifth floor. The secretaries were absent. They didn't typically care for football, so their tardiness was harder to dismiss. Daniel was a morning person, but he certainly wasn't the first to arrive each morning. The empty cubicles spoke to the contrary. The quiet office gave him a peaceful environment in which to check through the weekend's worth of missed emails. While he waited for Outlook to load and catch up, he pulled a CD out of his backpack. It settled into the DVD-ROM tray and popped up the PC's music player while Daniel got his headphones settled around his ears. The final sips of from his coffee mug came just after the last of the replies landed in his outbox. He paused the music, set his headphones down on the desk, and snatched his mug for a coffee run. The break room coffee machine had one full pot, but the mold indicated that it was from the previous week. He dumped it out and pulled a fresh carafe from one of the cabinets. While that brewed, he eyed the assortment of 1.50 pastries in the vending machine. As he contemplated making a bad decision, a desk chair rolled past the break room door. Daniel only caught a glimpse, an indistinguishable blur. He poked his out of the door to see Michelle, one of their former interns now a full time hire, pushing the wheeled chair around the office. " Um, " he started, aiming to get her attention. " If someone sees you... " She spun in place and giggled. " Who's gon na see me? " she asked, holding her arms out to highlight the empty building. " Everyone's probably still at home or buying supplies. Looks like we're the only ones stupid enough to spend our final moments in this hellhole. " " Supplies? " Daniel asked. " What do you mean ' final moments? " Someone doesn't read the news, " replied Michelle turning her attention to the ceiling spinning around above her. Daniel bolted over to his desk and pulled up a web browser. He didn't usually use the internet at work as it was frowned upon, but he had to know. As he read through headline after headline, Michelle had wheeled her boss's chair outside of his cube. " You can see it, too. " She pulled her seat towards the window. Daniel followed suit. The white light that found its way into his bedroom had grown more intense on the floor of the office. Daniel traced the light back to its source, what looked like a giant moon hanging in the sky, growing larger each moment. " Not too much longer, now, " Michelle noted. She looked more excited than scared. Daniel rolled himself back to his computer. He pulled open his email and clicked on Compose. He filled in the email addresses for his parents and Amber. The subject he skipped entirely. The cursor blinked in the main body, the software's tapping foot anxiously awaiting activity. But the words wouldn't come. Daniel couldn't think of anything to say. He didn't even think they'd read it if he had sent something. He closed Outlook and Firefox. The music controls sat front and center. He reached for his headphones. Instead of grabbing them, he reached beneath his desk and pulled the connector from the tower. When he clicked Play, his music played through the pathetic integrated speaker. He hummed along. " Who is that? " Michelle asked over Daniel's shoulder. " Janus Trio. They opened for Ra and Breaking Benjamin a couple of years ago. " " No way. I love Breaking Benjamin. " " I think I have a CD of them somewhere... " Daniel said, reaching into his backpack. " No, " Michelle interrupted. " I like this band, too. " She smiled and Daniel returned one in kind. " Can you turn it up? " she requested. Daniel maxed out the speakers, which was enough to at least fill the room with a tinny accompaniment. Michelle grabbed his hand and pulled them both back to the window. She stared up at her impending doom. Daniel focused his attention on her hand clasping his, then at her smiling face. Her head was bobbing to the music. Daniel reaffirmed his grip on her hand and he, too, looked up to stare at the massive rock. A smile overtook his face. It had been a pretty good morning.
