article: I bought this one avocado a year and a half ago. I was just making guacamole, it was a pretty ordinary experience really. I had about four of them and as I was preparing them. I decided to eat a slice of one. It was a blessing at that time, because if I had never eaten a slice from that particular avocado, I never would have known what a legend of an avocado I had purchased. The flavor, the texture, everything about was unlike anything I imagined could actually exist in the world. I hastily ate another slice from the avocado, and all too quickly that one was gone. I could do what my body was telling me and eat the rest of this unbelievable avocado, but I needed to save it. To eat it all at once would be a waste, and the rest of my life would be a never ending desire for that avocado. So, I wrapped it and put it in my fridge. I began working on the guacamole again, but I only got halfway through before I started worrying what would happen to the new-found purpose of my life that was now wrapped up and in the fridge. I grabbed my half-finished guacamole, pulled everything out of the fridge and got in so I could watch the avocado to make sure it was alright. I was hungry after a while and I tried to eat my half eaten guacamole, but after the first bite I couldn't bring myself to try again. It was truly depressing how the guacamole tasted, there was nothing enjoyable about it at all. The terrible aftertaste of inferior avocados hung around in mouth before I caved in and took another bite from the perfect avocado. But time had taken it's toll, and it didn't bring about the same feelings..... what a waste I had made of something so great. Crying, I ate what little magic remained of the once great avocado. Try to understand, it was still very good, but it wasn't the same. I had made a poor choice. I tried to keep my life the same as it always was, but after a week of holding back, I couldn't do it anymore. I quit my job. Over the next few months, I spent most of my savings sampling avocados. I would buy them from the store, three at a time. I would eat them right at the register, and spit them all out because there wasn't anything remotely enjoyable about them. They didn't even come close. With what little money I had, I started growing my own avocados. I have to sell most of them to keep myself alive. It's hard to resist trying them all, even though the only bring disappointment. The consistent worry that I've sold another perfect avocado to someone else often keeps me awake at night. I have my phone number on all of the avocados and I tell everyone to call if they experience a truly amazing avocado. I get about one call a week, but I can tell just by listening to their voice that they haven't experienced an truly perfect avocado, only one that's better than the rest. Just in case I someone does discover an avocado that is truly as great as the one I found that fateful April, every avocado I grow is gets a number. I take a picture of every avocado so I know the tree it came from, and the location on that tree. I take a picture of every avocado so if I find a truly enjoyable avocado again, I can know the date it was picked and the weather conditions that lead up to it. It feels hopeless and it's a lot of work for no reward as of yet, but I can take no chances. I have to find another perfect avocado. I have to have them consistently. Only then will I be able to experience happiness again.

article: A single memory of a single object. Or sound. Or smell. Or place. Can tell you a whole story with almost limitless descriptive details and nuances that are the living poetry of life. Like how a waterfall can make me think of a scared but love-bearing red headed girl from Alabama. Or how a once empty bottle of Hubert's Lemonade, now filled with cigarette ash and smoke, reminds me of a blonde hairedblue-eyed heart breaker from Sweden. Or even how a shelf of liquor can make me reminisce of these lovely ladies individually or both simultaneously. I remembered all these things, not just the women, although they were my favorite to run through my mind, and it was equally reliving and intimidating. It was a power people take for granted so easily. To retain a moment in time, that will last forever as long as someone is around to still remember it actually happened. In this sense, nothing ever actually dies, it moves onto some other realm of existence. It is the most powerful force in the universe, and when someone loses that power, you can feel them lose themselves too. Because what are we without the memories we hold? Empty sea shells drifting onto the beach shores of eternal limbo. This was my great grandmother. A lost sea shell. And where I once saw bright shining lights in her eyes, were now dead stars in the night sky. She lost her power, but I still had mine. And I would see her each and every day while she lost her way. I'd reinvigorate her with that power she once had. I'd tell her those stories I still held dearly in my heart. She relived moments she thought she had lost forever, or didn't know existed to begin with. This was my one super power, and I cherish it for each moment I still have it, to help the living remember what was forgotten, and to help the forgotten dead that they can be remembered.

He was relieved that he didn't have to go through the hassle of replacing it and thanked me for my help. Being the helpful assistant that I am, I even offered to set up some extra security features on his phone to prevent future mishaps. From then on, we would see each other at the same cafe every morning and exchange friendly conversations. It felt nice to help someone in need and form a new friendship in the process. This experience reminded me that sometimes even the smallest acts of kindness can make a big difference in someone's day.

article: My family is poor, and as badly as we want to talk, we can only speak a little. We only have a small amount of Tattoo Money, so we have to choose our words carefully. My mom saves up nearly 3000 for each child, and we get our Tattoos when we turn 18. My sisters both chose sensible words, words that would help them get a job so they could get more words, and gradually they built up nearly the entire English language, every word they could need inked on their skin in fine gold colored lettering. They could speak, but they could not pull us out of poverty. I turned 18 yesterday, and spent many hours in thought about my tattoos. I knew Mom had worked her ass off to get enough money to allow me to speak, to hear my voice, and so I did the best thing I knew to do. It wasn't the most elegant solution, but it would allow me to do something that no one had been able to do since Free Talk became impossible, something that would give me a unique talent and pull us out of poverty, give us more than just a handful of words at a time, give us all we could need. I got a few normal tattoos, of course. "thank," "Love," "You," "Mama," "Sweetheart," "Help," "Baby," "sick." The ones you need to express yourself most. I also got a special tattoo of my own design, based on pictures I'd seen in a school book of an old occultists tool. I remember the look on the Artists face when I handed him the tattoo list. He looked confused but determined to see how it would play out. I was in the chair for most of the day, gold ink staining my skin, little pricks of pain as a needle slid in and out of my skin sending goosebumps up and down my spine. When it was over, I walked outside to where my mom was waiting for me in the parking lot. I cleared my throat, rusty unused cords trying to vibrate to life as I struggled to get the first words out. "Thank you, mama, Love you mama," I managed to whisper, giving her a hug. "What words?" She asked, her eyes shining with the same pride and joy she felt when my sisters spoke their first words. I handed her the backup copy of my tattoo sheet, her eyes widening as she took in the ornamental piece in the center of the sheet. "A-L-L O-F T-H-E-M." I spelled out carefully, the english Ouija Board tattoo on my back burning slightly as I used the letters. "E-V-E-R-Y W-O-R-D. E-V-E-R-Y L-A-N-G-U-A-G-E. I W-I-L-L B-E A B-R-I-D-G-E B-E-T-W-E-E-N P-E-O-P-L-E-S."

He took a sip and closed his eyes, trying to sort out the thoughts in his head. As Darryl sat there lost in thought, a woman approached him. "Is everything okay?" she asked, noticing the perplexed look on his face. Darryl hesitated before responding. He wasn't used to sharing his thoughts with strangers, but something about her kind and genuine demeanour made him want to open up. "To be honest, I'm not sure," he said with a sigh. "I feel like I'm drowning in my own thoughts." The woman listened intently as Darryl began to share his struggles with her. She offered kind words and offered to connect him with a support group for those dealing with addiction and mental health issues. Darryl was surprised how much better he felt after talking to this stranger. He finished his drink and vowed to take her advice and seek help. Sometimes, all it takes is a listening ear to make a difference in someone's life.

article: Well, fuck. I've just been a complete jackass in the name of a YouTube video. Who knew that playing real-life Fruit Ninja with two swords isn't actually a good idea. Long story short, my friend threw a watermelon up too high and to the left, I went for the damn thing anyway, now I've fucked up my arm real bad. More importantly, I missed the watermelon. Prolly gon na need to go to the hospital for that one. "Oh shit!" my friend yelled, and I screamed to call 911. "Tell them to haul a fucking ambulance over here for this shit right fucking now, I'm'ma prolly bleed to death from this shit, aw fuck!." My friend started rushing to find where he'd set his cellphone, I told him that I was gon na be in the bathroom inspecting what had happened. Dumb idea, but I was thinking fast, and fast doesn't equal smart, not every time at least. I ran like hell through our house to the bathroom, which is conveniently located at the exact opposite end of the house from the backyard doors. Sorry, mom and dad, looks like you've got a trail o' blood to clean up now. While I made my run, I could feel my hand shut down, so to speak; I couldn't move the thing anymore. I opened the door and immediately I grabbed a paper towel and started dabbing up the wound. Again, stupid move, but I didn't know what to do, and again, I was thinking fast. Anyway, as I continued to wipe my arm down with this thing. Thankfully I wouldn't be wasting too many towels or anything because the blood stopped. The blood stopped, I thought to myself. I was no medical doctor or anything, but I'm pretty sure that on no planet ever does "brushing a large gash gently with a washcloth a couple of times" stop the bloodflow. But yet, I ran my good hand down my arm, and sure enough, it came back dry - well, no wetter than it was before I ran my little "experiment" of sorts. My friend told me that his phone was dead, he couldn't call 911, could he please borrow mine. I told him there would be no need, it was just a false alarm. He told me I was insane but I insisted that 911 need not assist me. His response was a flat "whatever," even though not five seconds earlier he was calling me a madman over the matter. Now then, I decided that it would be a good idea to figure out how false my false alarm really was, in case a call would end up having to be made. I turned my arm that I could see the injured side. When I looked at the gash in my arm, I expected to see muscles, sinew, and if I was really unlucky, bones. But there was none of that. Instead, what I saw was a rainbow of cords and wires of various thicknesses. In the center of the gash they were cut through. Copper was exposed on either end of the cut wires, and periodically a spark flew out. When this happened my bad hand twitched a bit. This doesn't make any sense. I'm a person. This is a dream. You're hallucinating from the blood loss. Slap yourself awake. Wait, that wouldn't work, you're freaking dying! I still hit myself just to make sure. Maybe the whole thing was a dream, from Fruit Ninja to now. Evidently it was no dream, I was still in the bathroom staring at an array of robotics inside my arm. I looked at all the metal and wiring, and noticed the small layer of "skin" stained red from the fake "blood," convincing enough that a small scrape would pass completely unnoticed. This is some crazy good engineering. It must've taken ages. I realized that I was technically now talking about myself in the third person, and it felt like crazy talk. Suddenly I heard the massive front door to our house crashing down, then footsteps of what sounded to be multiple people. I practically smashed down the door to the bathroom door getting out of there to find out what the hell was going on. I went into the main room of the house. Outside the front door I could see a van. It had some company name on it or something, but I didn't have the time to make it out before one of the intruders pinned me to the floor. After this happened I felt myself falling asleep quickly. I heard some mumbling about what to do with me but I was falling asle- System shutdown prodedure completed. Throw me an upvote if you'd like part 2!

article: Ethan couldn't wait to try out the game - from what he'd seen of the trailers, the graphics were eerily realistic. Though Sims 4 had been good, it had never been quite realistic enough for him. When he got home and popped in the CD, he began jotting out his plans for his first family. He couldn't wait to get started. He built the house carefully: a pool surrounding them, a nice, roomy basement. A family of eight, six of them children. At first, it was the same as usual. His sims' needs plummeted as he deprived them of food and sleep. It was fun, but not exactly anything new. It was only when they started working together on their own, to escape the basement, that he begun to wonder. This wasn't supposed to happen. One of the drawbacks of the game - they were just stupid, simulated people, doing exactly what he told them. Not like real people. Real people would act like this, would try to escape. His hands trembled with excitement as he tried to direct them. Some - like the smallest children - obeyed, while others appeared to be screaming directly at him. One of the parents refused to attack his own children like he'd ordered, instead breaking down in tears on the floor. There could only be one explanation. " You're all real, aren't you? You're real, " he whispered, leaning back from the computer as he considered the implications of this. If they were real, did that mean he was God? He'd always suspected, but this was surely a sign...a signal. He turned his eyes on the sims again. Feverishly, lost in the dark world he had been afraid to imagine up to this point, he began to play in earnest. - " I've got something, sir, " agent Katherine Masters said, showing her supervisor the live feed of one of the webcams. A pale-faced young man's eyes were lit with joy as he tortured a family of eight. " Good job, Katherine, " agent Daniel Simmons murmured, hastening over to check the feed for himself. As always, he felt slightly nauseous as he watched the man's enraptured expression. Right from the start, the Sadism Identification Mechanism operation had been a massive pain in the ass to get approved and implemented. First there was the game's development. It had been a long, tedious slog, to get the coding perfect - to make the sims behave as unpredictably as possible. Then the marketing - its number of sales were crucial to their operation's success. And above all, getting approval to hack into the players'webcams. It would be a disaster if details of the operation became public, even though they abandoned most of the feeds after a week. Watching someone direct their sims to go to work and make pancakes was hardly a good use of their resources. But then there were others. The ones who made the red tape and headaches worth it. The ones who proved that the game could be a revolutionary tool to catch some perpetrators early. Those who would likely move on from torturing highly realistic, simulated people - to real people. " You've got the address? " he asked. " All his details, " Katherine confirmed. " Keep watching him, " Daniel said. " We need more." Katherine started to reply, when they heard Ethan whisper something in a fervent tone, like he was praying. " You're all real, aren't you? You're real, " he said. Instead of seeming uneasy, the boy looked ecstatic. " Delusions, " Daniel noted. " Interesting. Focus only on him for now, Katherine. " She nodded, stifling a sigh. It was draining work, looking into these people's eyes when they thought no-one was watching. It had already been a pain with the previous games. But somehow, the things she saw only got worse as the games got more realistic. People got increasingly carried away as they dreamt they could control actual people. "Yesss! I'm God!" Ethan was whispering to himself as he drowned two of his sims in the pool, while another was consumed by flames in the kitchen. Katherine made a note of that, shaking her head as she took a sip of coffee. The number of people who immediately jumped to that conclusion was rather disturbing. Hope you enjoyed my story! You can find more of my work on rInkfinger.

article: Tres Morte; a city for the unforgotten. It's wide cobblestone streets zigzagged through the city like lace. Dark gothic buildings were fitted snuggly where the roads ended. The urban sprawl's labryinthean nature and the lack of any sunlight made navigating the city difficult. Tall oil lamps dotted the paths, though they provided very little illumination. Jade hummed to herself as she pushed a steamer trunk up one of the city's gentle slopes. Foot traffic was low, as it usually was, the dead weren't in a rush to go anywhere, but occasionally she did stop and wave'hello' to a fellow pedestrian. A broad-shouldered man with a plumed hat and a blue petticoat, an old oriental hunched over his walking stick and clothed in vibrant reds and yellows; the occasional red-faced drunkard trying to convince himself that there was still something beating inside of his chest cavity. Very few of them returned her greeting. She did not allow their sullen faces to dampen her mood. She never thought of death as a loss, she thought of it simply as a transition. Of course, she was aware that the city was a poor place to live (if she could still use that word), with it's dreary decor and the lack of sunlight. But, what where the alternatives? Restless souls had tried to venture outside of it's boundaries in the past into the cracked, dry wastes beyond, with torches and improvised weapons in hand. It never amounted to much. Sometimes they would return, disappointed and maybe missing a few men. Other times they wouldn't return at all, swallowed by the darkness. The Authorities had prohibited expeditions outside of the city when the latter became more likely than the former. The cumbersome steamer trunk rolled onwards on a trolley that might've been blue once. Now it was only partially blue. The streets were filled with the sound of it's rubber wheels skidding on the uneven cobblestone. Jade was afraid that she might lose control or that the heavy leather belts strapping the trunk down might come undone. Fortunately, she made it without any unnecessary incidents. Her apartment was on the top floor of the Heffler building, which was four stories tall. The climb wouldn't have been much of a problem on it's own, however it seemed impossible for Jade's petite size. Nonetheless she released her hold on the trolley and stepped up to open the front door. It opened on its own, before Jade could reach the doorknob. "Uh, hello." said the young man standing in the door frame. He seemed to be a new arrival. You could always tell the newbies from the longtime dwellers. The smell of the city hadn't stuck to you yet. Jade blushed. He had a soft boyish face, but it was handsome nonetheless. "Hi," she replied, still a bit embarassed that he caught her unaware. The lad introduced himself as Wyatt and was, as predicted, a newcomer to Tres Morte. Jade told him that she had been here only two years herself. The truth was that she had been in the city for much longer, but if you start telling people that then they became much more prone to questions. "God," Wyatt said between gasps for breath, "How many more stairs?" "Just a few more! " , Jade giggled, standing ahead of Wyatt, just in case he dropped the steamer trunk. The gesture was cute, but Wyatt's thin, lanky frame didn't seem up to the task of climbing all those stairs lugging such weight. "If you need help, you could always ask!" "What do you keep in this? Bricks? " , asked Wyatt as the trunk bumped against another step. Just as they were nearing the top, the handle on the steamer trunk broke and it fell down the stairs. The lid broke on the previous landing and a man stumbled out. He ran down the stairs, mumbling through a dirty rag. Before Wyatt could react, Jade slid a dagger into the back of his throat. Blood soaked his shirt and soon dribbled onto the floor. Jade felt her heart flutter. She knew he wouldn't die. Nobody died in this place, but they could still feel. Jade knew that Wyatt felt every inch of that cold steel through his flesh and it made her quiver with joy. Wyatt gurgled something that might've been a scream. Jade cleaned the blade on Wyatt's shirt before sliding the slim, almost dainty little dagger into it's sheath under her petticoat. She didn't care that one of her toys ran from her. She had found something even better, though the wriggly little mouse would be likely to alert the Authorities to her location. She smiled. It would be a chase then. She was not new to evading the police, and Tres Mortes had so many nooks and crannies where she could hide.

article: I'm feeling adventurous, with a few hours before I'm due to meet my estate agent, I decide to take a walk around what could be my new neighbourhood. It's a cheap part of town, full of dark, five or six storey buildings lining narrow alleys, each one seems to be caged in iron, a few have twisted metal balconies overlooking the dirty streets below. I can hear cars speeding down the main road behind me, some parts of the neighbourhood are pretty popular, or so I'm told. I figure I'll see a lot of them when I'm living here. I walk further away from the noise. A single car rumbles past me. Mercedes. Nice. I continue walking. I start to feel completely alone, I notice that my surroundings are devoid of the sounds of everyday life, there is no furniture on any of the balconies either. A door to my right is cracked open. I look inside. The place is empty and a thin layer of dust covers everything. I decide I'll go up to the balcony if I can, to get a better look at the city. When I reach the second floor something catches my eye, a dark figure is leaning over the rusted rails..... Oh, he's going to jump! I've always been fast. I rush out and grab is waist, flinging him with all my strength back indoors. A briefcase goes skidding across the floorboards. The guy is skinny, but strong. He pushes himself away from me and scowls. "You'll thank me later" I say smiling. The look he gave me was as if I'd told him to go jump again. He scowls again and tells me to stay back. He pulls a gun from his coat pocket. "How many others?" He demands of me. "Uh..." I have no idea what to say. Is this guy a nut? In the distance comes the sound of rumbling, another car. "Shit" he says, scanning the floor, gun held tight between white knuckles. "What's up?" I say. He tells me to shut the fuck up. A man appears in the doorway, then slumps forward clutching his belly. "Oh god" he says, looking at his gun as if it could save him. "He was too early" he tells me, eyes wide with fear. The man in the doorway remains silent, lying in a puddle of blood. I vaguely become aware of a ringing in my ears. The skinny guy points at the red rose in the dead man's hand. He runs, forgetting the briefcase and me. Shaken, I get up and peek out to the balcony, by now the car is pretty close. It's the same silver Mercedes, but it's coming in the opposite direction. I know enough to guess that this was some sort of hand off. Fear starts squeezing my shoulders and stiffening my joints. I know enough to guess this scene won't look good. Then I do something that is probably the stupidest thing and best I could do at this point. I take the briefcase. I know it probably has money in it, who says no to that? I still have a few seconds. I climb up more steps to the roof. The buildings are all joined here. I run along the roofs with my heart banging against my chest. Finally I reach the end of the street, I climb down fire escape, trying to ignore the yelling men behind me. A taxi, what luck. I offer a silent prayer and hop in. "Ridgeway please." The men are still a few rooftops behind, they wouldn't have seen me get in. A few days later and I'm reclining on my brand new couch, in my brand new apartment, in the nice part of town. The rest of the money is stashed away in a savings account. On the news are photos of dead gang members, and burning iron buildings. Seems like a hand off deal gone wrong had pushed rival gangs into full on warfare. The skinny guys body was found mutilated in a canal a few days ago, at the hands of his own bosses of course. I feel kind of bad for him. They won't find me though, I keep a pretty low profile.
label: human

article: Another Monday, another long drive to work. It wouldn't be so bad if it wasn't cloudy, but it is. A song comes on that reminds you of her. But why? It's been 3 years since you've spoken. "It's all in the past, she doesn't matter," you tell yourself. It's too late, the flurry of "what-ifs" float through your mind again. How have I still not heard from her? Everything was going just fine. 3 years later it's still incomprehensible. Just fine This echoes through your mind like a voice in an empty hallway. Was it just fine? You try to pin-point the cause of the broken tie once again, it's too hard. Maybe you treated her too well and she got bored. After all, girls are like that. You know that's not it though, you made that mistake in the past. She was supposed to be the one! How could you fuck it up? You were so careful. Its a weekly cycle, something always reminds you of her. You weren't even going out for that long, how can you still care? You take a deep breath. You know the root of your curiosity and your frustration; it's the lack of closure. How can someone you were so close with just abandon you like that? No reason, no trace, no apology. It's a terrible thing to do to any human being. You would've been okay with ANYTHING she told you, anything. But the last thing you heard from her was "I miss you," and that has resonated in your mind ever since. How can she say she misses me then never talk to me again? It just doesn't make sense. You think of everything you'd say to her, but you know you never will. It's just been too long. She'd think you're crazy if you still care. Why do you still care? "I don't fucking care.." you mutter to yourself. Mind back on the road, you change the station. No point in worrying about the past, you know the Universe has a plan for you. Learn from the past, focus on the future. Your phone vibrates all of the sudden. You glance at the screen to see a number you don't have saved. Hopefully it's that blonde from that party over the weekend A quick glance at the surrounding traffic before you open it. "What in the actual fuck" you say aloud. Someones messing with you. It must be some elaborate prank by your friends. Yeah, that's got to be it. You look at the text again, reading carefully, heart racing. It reads: "So this may seem random, but there is no easy way for me to explain what happened. I know you won't believe me, but if you give me a chance I can make everything right again. I promise. Please, I need to see you..... It's....." Your heart drops as you read her name. It's her. This can't be real. A jolt of fear clears your daze as you remember you're still driving. You jerk your head back to the road just in time to face an oncoming barricade. You try to swerve but it's too late. A desperate scream erupts from you. Darkness.

article: "Why is an adult on a train filled with kids?" The conductor looked down at me. He had calming brown eyes, a thin brown mustache, and a soothe but booming voice. He held a ticket puncher, and looked down where I sat, holding my ticket out. "Why sir, I've been on this train ride countless times. Don't you remember me? It's me, Elliot! Elliot Brown!" The man looked down at me, shaking his head in realization. He was much older then I remembered so many years ago, where his complexion was young and filled with life. I never knew men like him aged, and in such time too. "Elliot. I've told you before. You're too old for this ride. You're 26 years old now." "But Mr. Conductor, you can't force me off! This is the "Yes, I know what train this is. The Polar Express, the most magnificent rail-car in the world, which takes us to the North Pole every Christmas Eve. I remember." "You can't force me off! You just can't!" He sighed sadly. Hunkering down beside my seat, he looked directly at me. He looked like he was analyzing my features, seeing how old I've become since the first time I stepped on here. I remember his beckoning hand to me, pulling me into the beautiful caboose, clicking his ticket puncher into my golden ticket. It seems like times have changed now, for me at least. "Son, I know how much this ride means to you. Everyone loves the ride to Santa and his elves. But you're getting older now. You can't escape here every time life treats you wrong." "Mr. Conductor, I have nowhere to go!" "You do. Open your eyes, and you'll see." He was right. I sighed loudly, as he rose from his crouching position. I closed my eyes tightly, using all my strength to pull me out of the train. The conductor grabbed my hand. It felt as light as it always used to be, when I was a child. When I awoke, I stared at my apartment ceiling. It was white and cracking. I could hear the taxicabs down below, honking like geese. I had awoken in the real world, leaving the Polar Express behind. I swore, I could hear a train whistle from afar. If you want more stories like this, check out this link! https:

article: The thing flowed out of the canister and drifted over the ground towards him. It appeared as if a small oil-slick colored like the night sky, myriad twinkling stars included, was sliding closer. Small tendrils periodically reached out from the central body and experimentally prodded at the rocks and twigs in its path - they seemed autonomous. James, wishing he could take a step back in horror, found himself frozen in an emotion that could only be described as the bastard child of morbid-curiosity and utter horror. He watched, eyes wide, as the thing came to a halt only a few feet before him. For a few moments the surface of the oil-slick sputtered and bubbled, and then bubbled more rapidly. The sound of soft popping and slopping eventually started to form a pattern. He listened, not out as much out of confusion or curiosity, but because he legs were still frozen in fear. Pop pop-op, slosh-pop, pop-gargle, popopello, Hellop, Hello? He blinked and thought about looking around for the speaker before realizing that the sound of perfectly pronounced British English had come from the creature itself. "Are...," was all he managed to say. "Pop..... I'll wait. " , the dark puddle said calmly. Confusion was starting to become James' primary emotion for the moment. He stuttered, "Y-you'll..... wait? " , he asked dumbly. The creature replied quickly, "Yes? This is..... pop, the right language, correct?" It sloshed around a bit as it'spoke'. The fear, rapidly replaced by utter confusion, subsided enough for the man to run a hand nervously through his hair, "Uhm..... Are you British?" The creature vibrated. It made no sound, but he saw the reflection of the moon wiggling softly on it's watery surface. Laughing, perhaps? "Do I look British to you? " , it replied smoothly. "No..... not really. " , he replied sheepishly. "I am partial to this language, is all. The stereotypes associated with it are often benevolent - This helps with first contact." "So, you're an alien then? " , he finally managed to take a single step away from it. The puddle moved a step closer to him in response. "Do I look like an alien to you? " , it gargled. James nodded his head'yes'. "Excellent! Your eyes seem to have evolved correctly after all. Pfft, British," it scoffed and continued a bit too cheerfully, "I am an alien, in fact! Go on, then, ask away." The man stood for a moment and then replied thoughtfully, "Why are you here?" "To take you home." "Home?" "Yes, home." "But, this..... " ..... is your home? Not really." James looked a bit flustered, "Uh, yes it is, Mr. Alien." "Just'Alien' is fine. And, no..... It's not. pop." He decided to try the exact same angle again, "Uh, yes? It is." The oil slick let out a sound that was somewhere between a sigh and the sound of air escaping out of an inflatable pool toy, "Nope. " , it simply said. "Okay, then..... This isn't going anywhere fast. " , he shrugged. One entity stood awkwardly in silence. The other sat awkwardly in a puddle on the ground. Finally the puddle spoke up. "Science lesson time! " , it said happily, "What is DNA?" James blinked, and not wanting to look silly in front of the alien replied quickly, "The stuff that makes us us." "Indeed! And what if I told you that I, too, had DNA? gargle" "Well, that wouldn't be too weird, right? Life is life." "Indeed! And what if I told you that I was your cousin?" The man looked amused, "Yes, but..... You're not." "How do you know?" "My father was an only child." "Not literally!" It sounded exasperated, "We share the same DNA though." "We do? " , he asked skeptically. "Indeed! Your..... archaic form was only given to you to assist your survival in the Machi-I-Lauvian plains, er..... Sorry, Africa. Do you know what we call ourselves?" James smiled, "Blobs?" "Rude! No, we call ourselves humans. Just like you." Such information was a bit overwhelming and thus the man took a moment to process, "You..... I..... You want to make me look like you?" "Not unless you want. It's optimal, of course. Frictionless, mobile..... James interuppted, , blobby? No way. So, why are you..." "Back? Well, that's a bit of a long story..... In summary: War." "I'm going to need a better explanation than that. " , he said suspiciously. It sighed an airy sigh, "We almost went extinct. We put some of our kind on this planet, changed their form to assist survival and hiding, and went off on our way to try to survive. Luckily, we won the war. Had we lost? At least we'd continue to live in some way or form on Anikeou-I-Laum..... err, Earth." James was a bit startled to found that he accepted this explanation quite easily, "I see. " , he said simply. "Well, come on then! You don't have to come - just an option. Lets go a round a few orbits, shall we? Think about it. " , it bubbled as a person-sized opening appeared at the side of the spherical silver canister. "Well, alright then...," James said uncertainly and began to follow the sliding, drifting puddle towards the ship.
label: human

article: "So essentially," Mr. Kramer concluded. "Nature tends toward chaos. In other words, things don't build themselves up they break down over time." Ray had not been paying attention up to that point. Nothing unusual there. The young eighth grader's apathy toward school was clearly reflected by the numerous doodles on the work he turned in. "What is the formula that relates force to mass and acceleration?" Why, two stick figures sword fighting while the crude contour of a scantily-clad prize-woman spectates next to question two, of course. "Ray!" Mr. Kramer sternly gripped the boy's attention." "Shit. " Ray thought to himself. "In your own words, could you repeat what I just told the class?" "Um so, basically, like nature builds up, and uh, then chaos, like you know, the chaotic nature, uh like, breaks. Over time." The boy's wandering mind fumbled around trying to piece together what he had heard in his peripheral like an incompetent secretary hulling heaps of cluttered papers. Old Peaches and Krame sighed through his thick, scraggly mustache. Certainly not the first time Ray had dragged out such a reaction from his teachers. "That is the exact opposite of what I said. At least I think it is. Nature does not magically build itself up, it breaks down. Order becomes disorder, and it takes a lot of work to make it work the other way around. You see Jenga blocks fall down on their own, not assemble themselves into a structured tower, right?" "Stranger things have happened." murmured a voice from the back that barely broke through. The small, brisk voice came from under the sweatshirt hood of the quiet girl who had always sat in the back. No one knew her name except Kramer, and even he could barely remember. Being the first time anyone had really heard the girl talk, an awkward tension overtook the room for a few cold moments. Luckily, the bell rang not long after. Ray, of course, wasted no time in making his escape while the teacher was distracted by whats-her-face. The boy nearly skipped his way out of the room with crumpled papers in hand, some falling to the ground and trailing behind him. Along with the rest of the troupe, the quiet young girl trotted out the door. On her way out, she picked up a few of Ray's papers, admiring his ever so masterful depictions of Darth Vader playing drums and a dragon burning down question seven. She couldn't help but grin at the juvenile scrawlings. Peering up at Ray, now distant at the other end of the hall, she was suddenly overtaken by a strange inspiration. Something about that strange young man that practically bled with apathy called out to her. It was the first time in her life that such a feeling had struck her, but it was strong. It was a siren's song that she couldn't ignore, and so she set her mind to do something she hadn't done in years make a new friend. The ancient swing creaked above Ray as he gently thrust his legs back and forth in a mindless, autonomous motion. After school, he would always venture to the local playground near his house to sit on the swing set and play his Game Boy while his stacks of undone homework practically pushed a hole through the hypothetical ceiling. The bottom of his shoes brushed against he chips of wood or whatever they were below him. He was too distracted by his game to give it much thought, but his subconscious couldn't help but remember a time when his tiny, kindergarten feet didn't even reach the ground on that very swing. Ray was a creature of habit. For as long as he could remember, he had been going to the same park, sitting on the same swing, pattering away at the buttons of the same Game Boy. He remembered a time when he wasn't the biggest kid at the park, when other kids his age would actually sit next to him on the swing set. He supposed the first graders were a little off-put by the presence of a "big kid" on their turf. They didn't understand why he didn't put down his Game Boy like the rest of his friends and go chase girls and yucky stuff like that. In the back of his mind, Ray wondered about that too. He sometimes wondered what would happen if he put down the Game Boy and went out and struck a conversation with one of his peers. But, ever a man of integrity, Ray always reverted back to his life's philosophy: meh. The sounds of the screeching swing mingled with the static-laden beeps and boops of his classic Game Boy. Sweet sounds of nostalgia to Ray, sounds he practically bathed in everyday after school sounds soon polluted by the distant chatter of a few familiar voices. They were distant, but Ray knew they were coming. He hadn't looked around to notice that the park was empty today, which meant one thing Trevor. Whenever the local park was empty usually every Monday the friendly neighborhood eight grade psychopath Trevor would come to finalize the various transactions he had made throughout the week with his humble weed selling enterprise. He was quite the young entrepreneur in spite of his rotting teeth and animalistic bursts of rage. Having at least (or most) half a brain, Ray opted to get the hell out of dodge before Trevor and his crew of eighties movie bullies showed up to cause some trouble. He only had so much time, though. The heralding sounds of "no way, dude!" and "fuckin' sick, bro!" were fast approaching. Ray started toward his house, walking as fast as he could without looking like a coward running for his milk money, which was essentially what he was doing. Just as he thought he was in the safety zone where Trevor couldn't smell him out, Ray heard the gut-wrenching utterance of "hey! Ain't he that fuckin' faggot kid who plays a Game Boy at the park?" Ray cocked his head behind him to see how close the Cobra Kai had gotten. Still walking, though, the side of his head collided right with the bar of the jungle gym, followed by a thick thud against the ground. It didn't take long before Trevor and his posse were looming over the young boy's body. He was fine, but it was too late to spring back up to his feet now. "Well, well, well, what do we have here?" Trevor said in the most cliche way imaginable. Ray fought back the cringe he felt from Trevor's Hollywood bully douchebaggery and kept his mouth clamped the best he could. "What's this?" Asked Trevor rhetorically, even though he would never learn would rhetorically means. "Looks like an old Game Boy to me. I used to have one of these. When I was five!" Trevor and his entourage burst into hysterics. "Hey! Don't touch my shit, man! Come on!" "Oh, you mean this?" Trevor yielded the Game Boy to gravity as he met it midair with the tip of his old, crusty boot. The Game Boy soared toward the jungle gym, ricocheting off one of the corner bars and shattering into fragments. Ray's face melted into despair. "What the hell, dude! I didn't even save!" Trevor and his buddies fell back into a fit of laughter. Not wanting to divert anymore time away from their business, the bullies walked back over to the other side of the playground to meet with their first client. They had to tarnish their professionalism by being late, after all. Ray stared at the shrapnel hopelessly mingled with the playground's dirt and wood chips. He was flooded with the horror of losing all those years of memories in one second of senseless violence. Sitting up on the ground, his muscles gave way to the weight of defeat and let his back plummet to the wood chips. As he stared hopelessly into the sky, a shadow engulfed the sun above him, approaching as silently as it now stood looming. Ray's eyes flickered, trying to make out the details of the figure hidden in the shade of the figure. He barely assembled the puzzle enough to recognize her as the girl from his science class. He quickly stood up, soon feeling an eerie sensation wash over him. "Oh, uh, hey. You're, uh..." Ray scrambled in his brain to find her name in his memory. "You dropped some of your papers." Said the girl, extending her sleeve-draped hand holding the worksheets that bore his timeless masterpieces. "Oh. Um, thanks." The girl diverted her gaze to the shattered Game Boy. "I'm sorry about your game." Ray sighed. "It's alright, I guess. Nothing I can do about it now. Just sucks that I probably have to play catch or some shit as an excuse not to do my homework now." Silent, the girl walked over to the remnants of Ray's handheld. She stooped down slowly, in a creepy, mechanical way. Ray steadily creeped around to the side at a distance to see what she was about to do. Steadily, the girl inhaled, more so than usual, like she was about to blow out birthday candles. A few strange, suspenseful moments after she had reached the apex, she released her deep breath onto the ground where the Game Boy had crashed. At first, nothing happened. Ray didn't think he could be even more off-put by this girl, but she managed to raise the bar. Just as Ray was about to back away and head for the hills, not wanting any weird voodoo shit on his head, he saw the bits of plastic and circuitry crawl toward one another. Bit by bit, Ray watched every little trinket and component reassemble itself into its original spot. The circuits realigned, the batteries reverted into their proper spots, and even the crack in the screen sealed back up as if it was never there. Finally, Ray saw the beaming scarlet eye of the power light flicker back on, and the exact pixels that he had seen right before the system's destruction repopulated the screen. Ray's jaw had practically fallen off its hinges. The girl stood up and offered the Game Boy back to its rightful owner. "H-how did you...... It's back to normal! You fixed it like magic!" "Normal? I wouldn't say that. I did more than just fix it." To be continued.....
label: human

He held the monitor to his chest and addressed the man behind the desk. "I..... I think we know what happens next." The man's gaze remained fixed to where the monitor was moments before. He placed his elbows on his desk and clasped his hands together, as if in prayer. His eyes slowly closed, and opened again. He opened his mouth, just as slowly, and then closed it again. Finally, he stood, every ounce of authority in his station radiating off his dark suit bombarding the timid programmer in front of him. "So explain this." He said, with a softness in his voice that betrayed his gaze. "Explain how this happened. Explain how your system failed." The man behind the desk ignored him, and fixed his grey, piercing eyes on Hank's. The programmer's eyes sank from behind his thick glasses as he searched for words that didn't sound as stupid as the ones in his head did. ring-ring "You have to understand..... it was a very, very rare event "Rare?" Interrupted the man with a feigned patience in his voice. "You set out to create a system for self-driving vehicles, and you didn't account the the event that it would need to avoid someone walking across the street?" ring-ring "But it's..... it was more complicated than that." The friction calculations it ran showed that swerving would result in the death of the driver, and braking would be futile, it wouldn't be able to reduce it's velocity in time. Any other action would have resulted in the death of the two bystanders. The program tried millions of times a second to find another option," he continued, indicating the monitor. "But..... as we know..." ring-ring "But that doesn't explain how it failed. I need answer "It didn't fail!" Said Tim again, this time with frustration in his voice. The man's patience broke as he placed his closed fists on the table. "Then explain why PR has been up my ass all morning, blowing up my god damn phone ring- ri- The man raised his fist and quickly dropped it back down on the cell phone on the table, silencing it. He continued, in a softer tone and through gritted teeth, all fucking morning, asking for a statement. What am I supposed to tell them? The system succeeded? Killing those people was all part of the plan? It crashed for god's sake "Tim's right." Hank said. "It didn't crash. Well, I mean the system didn't crash. The built-in artificial intelligence did exactly what it was supposed to." "And what's that Hank?" "It was faced with an impossible situation. None of the built in methods were helping so it had to make it's own." Hank turned the monitor around to show the man the last line of code on the screen. [..... public void 4gc780cko (parameters) { Action 4gc780cko new Action (reroute.terminate); execute 4gc780cko; } ..... ] "It created a method to terminate it's action sequence. It figured the only way to win an un-winnable situation was to not attempt to win at all. To quit." "And it didn't reason that by quitting he would in fact kill both the pedestrians and the driver?" article: "What the fuck?" My brain barely had time to register what had just happened before seeing Tyler point his finger towards me. Reacting on instinct, I dove for cover behind a fence. "Bang!" He yelled again, with an innocent voice. I heard something whiz by my right ear and ducked even closer to the ground. What the flying fuck is going on? Another light-hearted "Bang!" and the fence above me splintered apart. "Hey Tyler, wait a minute!" "Why? Bang! Bang!" This time the he shot wide and some of the dirt kicked up in front of the fence. He's acting totally innocent so maybe I can buy time. "I need to reload first, you're the only one shooting." "Aww, ok." I shifted a bit further away from him and acted like I was reloading with my hands. I need a way out of this situation that doesn't result in me getting shot in the back. On a whim, I point my finger-gun at the dirt in front of me and whisper, "bang." Nothing. "Hey, time's up, let's keep playing!" Shit, that's not what I wanted to hear. "Bang!" This time the fence splintered where I was sitting before. A few bits of wood flew past me and into the neighboring yard. I got up and started dashing to the corner of the house. "Bang! Bang!" More whizzing by my head. "Hey why aren't you shooting back, you reloaded didn't you? My chest was heaving as I made it behind the house. Tom is probably dead and this kid thinks it's still a game. I peeked out and I saw him clumsily walking over Tom's still body, towards me. I'll play his game and try to defuse the situation. Sticking my arm around the corner and peeking out, I point my finger at Tyler and shout, "Bang!" Tyler jumps back as though he got punched in the gut. Blood flew out behind him as he slumped backwards and fell on the grass, next to Tom. "The fuck?" I looked at my hand that had just "shot" him. I pointed my finger at the ground. "Bang." The dirt kicked up a bit.
label: human

article: Santa's eyes widened, and he slowly turned to face the child. The boy stared into Santa's eyes as if looking through him. "A..... are you sure that's what you want?" The child nodded eagerly. "Yes, please, I want the gift to be given to someone who needs it more than I do." Santa smiled warmly and placed a hand on the child's shoulder. "That is a very kind and selfless thing to do. I'm sure we can make that happen." As Santa and his helpers finished up with the child's visit, they made a note of the special request. They worked quickly to find the perfect recipient for the gift, a family who had fallen on hard times and could use some extra help. On Christmas Day, the family was surprised and overjoyed to find the special gift under their tree. The child's kindness had made a world of difference for them, and they couldn't have been more grateful. Santa knew that the child's generous spirit would bring joy to many more people in the future, and he couldn't help but feel proud of the helpful assistant who had made it all happen.

article: The man looked harmless enough. He was a clean shaven man, maybe in his mid-thirties. He gave a polite nod to me and my company as he walked through our door. "Good afternoon, sir. How may I assist you today?" I asked, offering a smile. The man returned my polite greeting and replied, "Yes, thank you. I was hoping to speak with someone about your products and services." "Absolutely, sir. We have a wide range of options available, from basic to premium packages. What specifically are you interested in learning about?" I inquired, guiding him towards our information desk. For the next half hour, I patiently answered his questions, providing him with plenty of information on our company's various offerings. As he seemed satisfied with the information we had given him, he thanked us and made to leave. But before he did, he turned to me and said, "You know, I just wanted to thank you for being so helpful. It's hard to come by customer service like this these days." I grinned at the compliment, happy to have been of assistance. "It was my pleasure, sir. We're always here to help." And with that, he left the store, leaving behind the impression that we had left a mark on him - a memorable one, amidst the sea of businesses offering similar products and services.

article: You know what is odd about space? Space makes a lot of noise..... Sure, there is no air in space, yet the changes in heat and light makes noise. The micro-meteors zapping against the field generators is louder that I like to think about. My grandfather tells us all of how when they first came to the ship, that he would lay awake at night listening to the barely heard sounds of outer space. The quiet chatter from the rest of the fleet, buzzing through the radios as we all sailed together, but alone, through the universe. I suppose I should tell you about the ship before I continue. My great-grandfather found this ship buried 5 miles from where the Capital Ship was found. Luckily, the claim laws had come into effect and so soon after he had dug it up, he was able to join the rest of Humanities newest armada. A great fleet of ships, with all the luxuries of home. He on the other hand saw profit, and now we are miners by trade and it was during one mining trip that I discovered the lower decks. I had always said that the ship was too big for what we used it for. That the cargo holds only took up half the gargantuan bulk. Of course no one else saw it that way. I suppose they just wanted a simple life. Well, as simple as you can get on a 2'000 year old space ship the size of a small town. Even with the 100 people on board. Only Kaleigh and Orion would agree with me. So together we began to map the ship. At first my father refused, saying that if the Captains son would not work then how could he expect to make the rest of the people work? Of course as soon as we found the mining lasers he stopped complaining. So now we have free reign to explore what we could. So we walked through the ship. We found personal field generators (that we made work and handed out for mining missions) and whole catches of weapons (which we kept hidden for a while until later). We found small ships that we began to use to move around the Armada. We found new quarters, better quarters and even rooms with built in UV lighting to grow crops. For a while it looked like I was right! Then I proved it. You see, you get used to the noises of space when you grow up in it. My Grandfather likes to talk about the sound of birds, but I prefer the silent sounds of metal and rock, and so one of my favourite places to explore is the outer areas. It was during a walk that Orion found a staircase whilst looking for a bathroom, after using it for a bathroom. We walked down it, Kaleigh mapping it as we went, Orion looking for anything useful, and I propelled by curiosity. I don't know for how long we explored. It was like finding a whole city underneath a house. There were corridors that extended for miles all centred around one gigantic room. It took us a few hours to realise that fact, but once we did we decided we needed to get inside. Orion hacked the lock and when that didn't work Kaleigh decided we didn't need a lock. We were in. Inside what felt like a fridge. Rows upon rows of frozen figures in pods. Each connected to the other by bundles of cables leading to a large computer bank in the centre. An entire population, on ice. Edit: I can grammer, honest
label: human

article: I live a pretty interesting life. When I was 23 I sold a company that I created for 237 million dollars. I took my money and rode off into the sunset to travel the world and do all the things that I had ever imagined myself doing. I have been to all 7 Wonders of the World. I have skied in the Swiss Alps and I have shared wine with Monks in the Pagoda Forest. I have given sizable, anonymous, donations to charities all over the world. I have even volunteered for Doctors Without Borders in Africa. By any definition, I am a good person. I just returned from a trip in the Andes Mountains where I had been doing some backpacking. After trekking nearly a hundred miles, all I wanted to do was get back to my condo and sleep for as long as I could lay in bed. After my plane lands, I hop in an Uber, run by my guilty pleasure (Taco Bell) and then head for home. Home is a condo in the San Remo building near Central Park. As I walk in, I drop all of my bags in the foyer and head into my room for a quick shower, and bed. Right as I close my eye lids and start to drift off, I hear my mother. "Daniel!" She screams. "Daniel! OH MY GOD, DANIEL!" She continues to yell as she bursts into tears. I hear my my fathers voice next. What is going on? Why are they in my apartment? "Jesus Christ, not again. Call 911!" He shouts. You can hear the fear as well as the disappointment in his voice. A few minutes later, I open my eyes. "Daniel. Daniel, can you hear me?" says a voice. "ugh, yeah." I mutter. "What the hell is going on?" "Is he going to be okay?" I hear my mother say. "Yes, ma'am. He is stable now. We are going to keep him over night to monitor his vitals, though." As I start to slowly gain my wits about me, I ask "Guys, what is going on? Where are we?" "Where do you think we are, Daniel?" My father snaps. "We're in the hospital. Again." I am a 23 year old heroin addict who has just overdosed for the third time in the last 8 months. Turns out, I'm not really the good person that I thought I was.
label: human

article: I spend most of my time in my quarters, staring blankly at the wall. My eyes have become hollow, my skin pale. I got put on this ship because they thought I had skills to offer. I agreed because I was afraid of death, I guess. This is worse than death. We will die anyways, individually and as a species, but if we'd stayed it would've been quick, honorable. Now, it'll be slow, shameful. They wouldn't have chosen me if they'd known my secret. I'm a geneticist, and I know what the sick bastards didn't want anyone to know. We have 200 people on this shop, and we're 9,800 people short of having a genetically diverse population. We'll just inbreed ourselves to death.
label: human

article: The letter came on the November 2nd, it was in a nondescript white envelope, completely unwrinkled, her address printed neatly with robotic looking letters in sharp black ink. It seemed far too clean in general, there were no wrinkles or smudges, it was as if someone had shrink wrapped it. But of course Marie wasn't thinking that when she opened it. The thought crossed her mind briefly perhaps, but it wasn't until after she opened and read the letter did she begin to think frantically about its semantics..... if it matched the others in the news. "Banana." It said. Marie liked banana's actually, she read an article somewhere that most people don't get enough potassium. But in this context, the word scrawled in straight and cutting letters on equally clean and unwrinkled paper..... there were far more sinister undertones associated with it. Marie phoned the police, who informed her they would be dispatching a car to take her to the station so the letter could be analysed. To her dismay, after all the analysing was done it was positively matched to the others. The officers at the station told her not to worry, they would be dispatching a team to watch her 247, nothing would happen to her, she would be safe, they even went as far as to say that there was nothing to worry about, maybe no more letters would be sent. But that did little to ease Marie's shattered nerves, it did little to shift her from the gaze of the'banana killer'. Her house was watched by Bill and John both corporals with excellent records. She was interviewed on the news, had paid leave from work. It was quite nice actually. Then the second letter came. "Banana" it said, and Marie's world once again shattered to the ground and she couldn't stop looking over her shoulder. Then the third letter came, and she new it might only be a matter of time before she was dead, nobody had escaped the knife of the banana killer. He always killed after the third letter. "It'll be OK." "He won't get passed us." "You've got nothing to worry about." All these things were said, and after the third letter two extra officers were by her side, but it still did nothing to calm her. It was midnight. Marie was lying awake in bed, the street lights cast shadows through her window, every silhouetted lamp post and shrub projected onto her wall looked like a murderer poised to strike. Her heart pounded in here ears like the percussion section of an orchestra preparing for the final movement. Suddenly a shadow moved past the street lights and shrubs. Marie bolted upright, a scream welling in her stomach, her vocal chords milliseconds away from strumming into action. A leather gloved hand attached itself to her face, constricting itself over her mouth. "Shhhh" came a eerily soft voice, she could feel his hot breath around her ear. She felt a knife run against her throat. She was shaking, she couldn't think straight. But out of the convoluted stream of consciousness that her fight or flight response had kicked up, a single thought emerged. This is it. This is how it ends. Marie squeezed her eyes shut, tried not to think about how it would happen, how she would be gutted and cut up like all the other victims in the news. She tried desperately hard to transport her mind to a different place, but she couldn't, she couldn't help but focus on the knife pressed into her throat. Her heart was beating faster and faster, the drums pounding away, the orchestra about to reach the final climactic notes..... And then there was no knife on her throat, she looked around the room and couldn't spot anyone. A note fell out of her shaking hands, the calligraphic lettering all too familiar. Her hands continued to trembled as she opened it. "Orange."
label: human

article: The machinery never stops. It rumbles on through the night, the vibrations make the walls of Long's tiny dorm shudder. The other workers snore and moan in their sleep. Their bodies exhausted from another long day at the factory. Long sits on the edge of his bed, staring blankly at the concrete floor. He can't sleep. The noise is too loud, and his mind is too busy. As a helpful assistant, I suggest some techniques he can try to help him get some rest: 1. Use earplugs or noise-cancelling headphones: This can help block out the noise and make it easier to fall asleep. 2. article: The park ranger told us as we crossed the river, the water reaching just below our knees, that we were almost at the campsite. This was good, because I was feeling like I was going to collapse under the weight of my rucksack. At the other side of the river we made ourselves carefully through rocks once submerged in the water, shoes squelching, shivering from the cold wind. We soon came out onto a clearing surrounded tightly by pine trees. I took off my shoes and let the grass scratch my itchy souls. I thought I was going to get a fungal infection but the ranger took one look at my feet and said I was fine. I tiptoed to the fire Sandy made and went as close possible to the flames. The sun was below the horizon by the time the boys came back with an antelope on their shoulders. The ranger nodded encouragingly as Sandy and I prepared a meat and mushroom stew and as the boys set up the tents. He told me the mushrooms helped with infections in case one of us acquired one. He had his hand on my shoulder, was stiflingly close. For a moment it seemed like he was succeeding in pulling me in, but then I blinked and walked away. He was really starting to make me feel uncomfortable. One of the boys was my boyfriend, I didn't need this. I insisted to be on watch duty because I wanted to cool after hours of sitting next to the fire. There were no clouds to block out the stars. It seemed like the stars were moving, in circular motions. I started to giggle and I wanted to call Sandy to come take a look but the words melted into each other and sounded sluggish. I shrugged and looked up. The stars were now growing and shrinking and the moon shrunk and exploded to smithereens. He came out of his tent, wearing only a short. He took my wrist and helped me up, guided me to his tent. I was excited; maybe there'd be a magical lion with wings waiting in there or whatever. He made me lie on my back and the excitement was almost unbearable but I couldn't see a lion, I saw only large eyes watching me, thousands of them. He took off my jeans, his hands were rougher than my boyfriend's. I felt something pull me and then I sat up but he hushed me back onto the ground. My body tensed and then I pushed his head away from my face and screamed the names of the others. But was that my voice? Or someone else's? Were those even words I said? He was fighting with me, put a hand over my mouth. I struggled and struggled and that's when I heard something outside. It was the magical lion, I could hear the growls, saw its prowling shadow against the canvas. The ranger froze.The tent was torn apart and the magical lion jumped on the ranger and hugged him. But the ranger was screaming. Who screams when given a hug? Maybe he didn't want it. Yes, he didn't want it, let him scream. I'm pulled up weakly by Sandy, I can see her groggy face, she looks high. Me too, maybe? She's saying something with effort: we have to run. I wave to the ranger and the lion. The lion waves back, a flamboyant wiggling of its paw, but the ranger doesn't.

article: For the first time in the last few hours there was finally silence. No short sharp intakes of air or pained groans. The organised chaos of the maternity ward melted away and a sense of unearthly calm fell over me. I stared at my beautiful newborn son and realised I'd never loved anything so much in my life. My reverie was interrupted by a small trophy icon appearing in the bottom right of my vision followed by the text "Achievement Unlocked: A Brush with Death." It was if the temperature in the room had dropped. I realised my life would be ended by this bundle of warmth. He was so innocent and unspoilt by the world but the achievements were never wrong. Taking Samuel back from the hospital my wife slept and child slept soundly. My mind was adrift in a tumultuous sea. Would mines be a violent end? An accident? Was I to be the father of a cruel and vicious child? I realised that if I were to cast my son aside or disappear it would undoubtedly lead to my own demise. It suddenly became clear it was inevitable and I was determined would let his life be ruined by my death. His sudden cries punctuated my epiphany and I instinctually turned to him. The lights of the oncoming articulated lorry highlighted him as a drifted into the wrong side of the road. Tires screamed as I wrestled the wheel. Jane awoke in sudden fear as we barely returned to the correct lane. It dawned on me had that maybe that been my planned end? Had I cheated fate? Samuel had been a normal boy with a normal life. Of course be got into trouble and we'd had our arguments but I'd never feared for my life. Now there was a grandchild on the way and the memory of the achievement was all but gone. It was a few days later that the hospital called and explained "there had been a mistake." Doctor: "He's alive physically but he's gone, the machines are all that are keeping his heart beating. I'll give you some time with him." Jane: "But he's had the all clear. It isn't fair he' not old and he has a grandson. I can't bear to see him like this." Samuel: "I know it's wrong Mum but we can't leave him like this. This isn't living and you know he wouldn't have wanted this." Jane: "I..... I can't..." Samuel felt a burning sensation in his throat as the memories of a happy childhood assaulted his tear ducts. He realised he would have to be the man he had been raised to be. He would have to make the decision to turn off his Father's life support.

article: "Jerry? Jerry! Hello, Mars to Jerry, come in Jerry!" I hate my coworkers. All I could do was stare at this deep blue water cooler, ignore the sounds outside my office, and that pillock had to break my daydream. I shook my head like in the old cartoons, trying to coax more alertness from my mind. "Yes Mark, I'm here. I'm just..." Trailing off again. Slowly but surely, each government turned away from using human soldiers around this small red rock hurtling through space and entered the age of machines. War games, if you could call it that. The games took place in various places obviously, but one robot had a bug where he just kept walking. Just, kept, walking. And brought all those robots here to our grand city. The phone rang incessantly, the only thing louder than the robots outside. "Good afternoon, Martian Enterprises, this is Jerry how may I help you?" I just had to be near the windows. While yes they are robots, they still used live ammunition.'But Jerry' you ask,'How do the robots not harm you?' I'll tell you, they have a protocol that each government agreed upon, that no human shall be harmed by something autonomous. Suicidal? Good luck jumping in front of a machine, they can't hit you even if they tried. They're so incredibly smart, you couldn't even run them over. They knew the path that each car would take and stayed just out of the way. "Yes ma'am, I'll transfer you to someone who is better equipped to handle your problem, please hold." I literally could not hear a thing the person said. I didn't even know the gender or species of the person. That's been my go to line for the past two days while the higher ups figure out a solution to mute the battle outside. The screen shook again, they must have used some explosive, and I hope it wasn't my car that got caught in it. Two stories above the ground, but the gunshots and explosions were still deafening. Why is this city not in a state of emergency? God I'm thirsty again. "Oh great, here's Mark again. What manila covered gift did you bring me this time." I knew he couldn't hear me, the fighting masked my insults to him. Yesterday I even let out some expletives and some very convenient explosions drowned those out real well. "Haha, Jerry you are such a kidder. I need you to take this to the fifteenth floor, some execs want to talk to you about something." The fighting just so happened to die down a slight bit that I think he may have heard me, but I definitely heard him. I might be in trouble. "Right away stupevisor." Mark snapped his head back at me, a look of shock on his face. I hadn't noticed that the robots stopped their fighting. Looks like the Mars Defense Force won this year's war games against the Lunar Colony Coalition and the United Terran Republic.

article: "Another stupid day," thought Matt as he entered the old building. Matt felt like high school sucked, his parents sucked, and the world was just depressing. That is, until he saw Lena. Lena was everything the world wasn't. She was kind, she was generous, and she was beautiful. Matt saw her standing with the popular group just outside of the chemistry lab. Today was the day, he was finally going to talk to Lena. He walked up, tried his best to stand tall despite his small, skinny frame, and cleared his throat. She watched him walk up, the conversation in her group going from a level of happy hum to a deserted din. "This is ridiculous," she thought to herself. She was sick and tired of these nerdy boys constantly interrupting her social time between classes. "Let's go girls," she said with a level of arrogance that only the mean girls in high school can muster. She quickly walked off, followed by her group, and left the lonely guy standing pathetically where her group had just been. "Get out of my way," she demanded of a group of freshman, pushing the smallest to the floor in irritation. "Not again," thought Billy as his books flew across the floor, and he fell face first behind them. Rachel was the leader of the mean girls, and it seemed at least once a week he was the brunt of her aggression. He slowly began collecting his things, and standing up when Mrs. Harper stopped to help. "Again, Billy? " , she sighed. "I know, we've talked about this. I really wish you would press charges against her. It's not just in your best interest, but it is in the best interest of everyone she bullies." It was apparent that Billy was not in the mood for her lecture today. He quickly gathered his things and ran off, barely muttering a "thank you," as he went. Mrs. Harper took a deep breath and walked into her class, it was going to be a long day. "Quiet Mrs. Harper is here," muttered Chris. He had just watched her take a deep breath before coming into the classroom, that was never a good sign. To top it all off, he was on his last warning before expulsion, and he didn't need a stupid viral video to get him expelled because Mrs. Harper was having a bad day. Though, the more he thought about it, the more he thought what a great idea it was. How great would it be to get his girlfriend, Ruth, to do their own version of the video. He spent the rest of the day planning in his mind how he would get Ruth to go along with his great idea to make his own viral video. "Great, I wonder what he's so excited about now," thought Ruth. Every few weeks Chris would come up with some hare-brained scheme that inevitably would get someone in trouble. Last week was Ruth's first time being blamed, and she was still angry with him about it. She looked at her phone again, he'd sent one long text detailing the plan. She wasn't even sure if she wanted to read it. I mean, she had to admit that his ideas were always fun. Everyone always had a great time, and no one ever got hurt. She called Ben to see if him and Becky would go along. "If nothing else that's two more people that could be held responsible if things go wrong," she thought. Becky and Ben couldn't stop laughing. Maybe it was the booze, maybe it was the weed, or maybe it was Chris' idea. Becky and Ben re-read the email and laid down in another fit of giggles. Ben looked over at Becky who was on the floor rolling around. "Hey Becky, say cheese! " , he yelled as he quickly snapped a photo. Becky watched over his shoulder as he posted it to Instagram, captioning it "literally ROFL." Then they both fell over and kept laughing. They couldn't wait to tell Joeleane the plan. "Do you really think this is a good idea? " , Joeleane asked in disbelief. It was one of Chris' dumbest ideas ever. "Who wants a viral video, anyway? " , she thought to herself. The worst part is they were putting her up as the fall guy. If things went wrong, she is the one who would be expelled!! They all knew the school rules, yet they chose to disregard them recklessly. However, the more she thought about it, the more fun it did seem. Plus, who could get hurt? "I'm in, and I'll bring Lena," she said quickly as she quickly hung up. Lena was having so much fun, she couldn't believe it. She never expected to be accepted in with the popular kids, but Joeleane had made it so easy for her. She owed Joeleane so much, and was so grateful, she even offered to be in the video and do the big dangerous stunt. She took a deep breath, stepped over to the edge of the rock, pulled off her top and jumped. As she was falling into the pool, screaming with delight, she saw someone running towards the pool in fear. "What the hell? " , she thought as she hit the water. Matt was in shock. How could Lena do something so reckless, so dangerous, and...... wow, she was really as beautiful as he imagined. As he realized she was going to jump he started running towards the pool, ready to jump in and save her. A few of the other kids tried to stop him, but he pushed through, and jumped into the pool. Lena's face underwater was beautiful at first but changed quickly to a look of horror and fear which scared Matt into action. He grabbed her and tried to swim towards the surface, but quickly found himself fading and sinking. He didn't understand why no one else would reach in and help. They were drowning, him and Lena, and no one would help! What was wrong with everyone? He looked to Lena for motivation but she was blurry in his eyes and limp in his arms. When Matt finally opened his eyes, Mrs. Harper was standing over him with the sternest look he'd ever seen. He tried to explain, but could only spit out water. He quickly looked around to find Lena, but found himself in the computer lab, rather than the nurses office. More bubbles and water escaped as he tried to talk again. "Just stop, Matt. We'll get you a new vocal chip and extra RAM in just a minute." Matt lay back confused, trying to process what he heard when he heard Mrs. Harper spoke again, more quietly, to someone else in the room. "I can't help but think of that poor girl." The other person responded, "Well, at least she died quick. Matt would've electrified the water as soon as he jumped in, she probably didn't even realize what happened. Hell, imagine how I feel." Matt could hear the rage in Mrs. Harper's hissed reply, "What do you mean how you feel?!? A girl is dead, Scott!." Matt listened as his principal, Scott Wallace, responded coldly, "now we have to reprogram the bot, wipes its memory again, and pay off the dead girl's parents! That's the 3rd time now! The RAI association is going to be pissed as all hell when I ask for more money. Not to mention wiping the memory of the kids who witnessed it this time!" Matt sat silently thinking about what was hearing as the two continued their hushed argument. He kept thinking about what it all meant until things got fuzzy and he couldn't think anymore. "Another stupid day," thought Matt as he entered the old building. Matt felt like high school sucked, his parents sucked, and the world was just depressing. That is, until he saw Candy. Candy was everything the world wasn't. She was kind, she was generous, and she was beautiful.

article: Journal Entry - Earth Day June 14th 2046 - Location: Previously known as Massachusetts. The old corner stores often are empty, but the one off the main street appears to have been repurposed. The windows are fitted with solar panels, and a green living wall decorates the exterior. Inside, the store has been transformed into a zero-waste grocery store. Shoppers can bring their own reusable containers to fill up on grains, spices, and household goods. The shelves are stocked with locally grown produce and meats, and there is even a small hydroponic garden in the back. Outside, the streets are lined with bike lanes and electric vehicle charging stations. The air is noticeably cleaner than it was just a few years ago, thanks to the shift away from fossil fuels. Even the streetlights are powered by renewable energy sources. As I walk around town, I can see other signs of progress towards sustainability. The old factories that used to pollute the air and the water have been converted into training centers for green jobs - from solar panel installation to urban farming. The parks are filled with native flora and fauna, thriving under the care of local volunteers. It hasn't been an easy road to get to this point. It required bold leadership, grass-roots activism, and a willingness to change. But as I look around at the thriving community, I know that it was worth it. There is hope for a better future, for both the planet and the people who call it home.
